issues.body:
🤖 Comparison of the Marin 67B-A2B checkpoints from #6044 and #8813 against Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base, scored the same way lm-eval scored the open-weight baselines in #8824.

## TL;DR

- On the Paloma test split, the 65k-context checkpoint (step 156k) gets **0.7812** macro BPB and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base gets **0.8397** (−7.0%). Our model is lower on 15 of 16 subsets; M2D2 S2ORC is the exception (+2.4%).
- On the 7 legacy UncheatableEval subsets, it gets **0.5178** vs **0.5245** (−1.3%). We are lower on Wikipedia, BBC News and AO3. Qwen is lower on C++ (by 5.7%), arXiv Physics and arXiv CS; Python is a tie.
- Against Gemma 4 26B-A4B, the pre-trained base (`google/gemma-4-26B-A4B`; the instruction-tuned model is the separate `-it` repo), the 65k checkpoint gets **0.7812** vs **0.8100** on Paloma (−3.6%). Our model is lower on 12 of 16 subsets; Gemma is lower on C4 100 domains, 100 subreddits, Gab and Twitter AAE. On the 7 UncheatableEval subsets Gemma is lower: **0.5138** vs our **0.5178** (ours is 0.8% higher). We are lower on GitHub Python, arXiv Physics and arXiv CS; Gemma is lower on Wikipedia, GitHub C++, BBC News and AO3. All Gemma numbers are our own lm-eval run, not #8824's (see "Gemma: correction to the #8824 numbers").
- **Correction:** an earlier version of this issue used #8824's Gemma Paloma macro of 0.8494 and reported our lead as −8.0%. Run through our lm-eval setup, Gemma gets 0.8100. The difference is concentrated in short-document subsets (Twitter AAE 2.564 vs 2.016, Gab 1.469 vs 1.287), so #8824's Gemma setup differs from ours in a way that isn't context length. Qwen's #8824 numbers do reproduce under our setup.
- At 32k context, Paloma macro is **0.7716** (ours), **0.8278** (Qwen, −6.8%) and **0.7837** (Gemma, −1.5%). Gemma gains more from the longer context (−3.2%) than ours (−1.2%) or Qwen (−1.5%). UncheatableEval does not change, because every document fits in 4k tokens.
- The 262k context extension (qk_mult 1.75, 8× long-document skew, step 157k) is slightly lower again: 0.7795 Paloma, 0.5171 UncheatableEval.
- Marin's in-training Paloma numbers are not directly comparable to the #8824 open-model rows: Levanter scores Paloma **val**, lm-eval scores Paloma **test**, and Levanter packs documents. See "Why earlier Marin numbers differ" below.

![BPB per eval: 65k ckpt, 262k ckpt, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base, Gemma 4 26B-A4B base](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/e5caad072b27080a4b034e2c683beb1029032277/experiments/grug/moe/eval_67b_a2b_vs_open_bases_bpb.png)

## Results

## Method

The scorer reimplements lm-eval 0.4.12 `loglikelihood_rolling` for grug checkpoints. Evalchemy pins upstream lm-eval v0.4.12, and Qwen's run used the stock `local-completions` backend with `max_length=4096`, `tokenizer_backend=huggingface`, `tokenized_requests=True` (from its results JSON).

- **Documents:** scored one at a time, nothing packed. Paloma test split (revision `65cd6fc`, 154,440 docs); UncheatableEval Sept 1–14 2025 dumps (7,052 docs).
- **Windows:** lm-eval's API backend uses `max_length - 1` and rolls with `max_length - 1` again, so windows predict 4,094 tokens, each conditioned on the single preceding token, except the final window of each document, which keeps a full 4,094-token left context. The window code was checked against lm-eval's own `get_rolling_token_windows` + `make_disjoint_window` for lengths 0–30,000.
- **Tokenization:** HF tokenizer with `add_special_tokens=False`. The prefix token is BOS when the tokenizer has one (Marin: `<|begin_of_text|>`; Qwen has no BOS, so lm-eval used `<|endoftext|>`).
- **BPB:** summed NLL ÷ UTF-8 bytes of the document text, per subset; macro is the unweighted mean over subsets (matches Qwen's reported 0.839683).
- **Model:** params-only restore on a v4-64 in us-central2, bf16 compute. Before scoring, each job checks `qk_mult`, width, depth, expert counts, sliding window, `disable_long_rope` and `disable_pko` against the training run's `.executor_info` and fails on any mismatch (65k ckpt: qk_mult 1.57; 262k ckpt: 1.75).
- **Qwen numbers:** taken from the #8824 results file [qwen-results.json](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/hero-open-weight-ppl/2026.09.05.1/qwen-results.json). A rerun of Qwen with lm-eval 0.4.12 reproduced them (Paloma 0.8404 vs 0.8397, UncheatableEval 0.5246 vs 0.5245; [W&B run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lz5m5lk3)).
- **Gemma numbers:** our run of `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B` revision `24548b6` with lm-eval 0.4.12 `local-completions` (`max_length=4096`, HF tokenizer, tokenized requests) against vLLM 0.30.0 on 8×H100, on the same 154,440 Paloma and 7,052 UncheatableEval documents: [W&B run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/3rzcpy9e) (lm-eval results JSON attached). This is the same setup that reproduced Qwen.

## Reproduce

```bash
git checkout 9cb1640a79
# one job per checkpoint; each runs Paloma (test) and UncheatableEval as two child jobs on v4-64 us-central2
.venv/bin/iris --cluster=marin job run --no-wait --region us-central2 -e WANDB_API_KEY "$WANDB_API_KEY" \
    -- python -m experiments.grug.moe.eval_67b_a2b_step156k_paloma_lm_eval_rolling step156k
.venv/bin/iris --cluster=marin job run --no-wait --region us-central2 -e WANDB_API_KEY "$WANDB_API_KEY" \
    -- python -m experiments.grug.moe.eval_67b_a2b_step156k_paloma_lm_eval_rolling skew8
git checkout e5caad072b && uv run --with matplotlib python experiments/grug/moe/plot_67b_a2b_vs_open_bases_bpb.py bpb.png
```

Each child job takes 5–15 minutes once the slice is up. The 262k job ran exactly this commit. The 65k job ran an earlier revision of the same file with identical scoring code but without the startup config check; its config was checked separately (qk_mult 1.57).

## Context length: 4k vs 32k

All three models rescored with lm-eval `max_length=32768` (ours: same grug scorer, [W&B Paloma](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_step156k_paloma_lm_eval_rolling32768); Qwen: [W&B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/rfqtrvbi); Gemma: [W&B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/qtfi2lqk)). The 4k columns are our own runs of each model; Qwen's 4k column is the rerun, not #8824. Only documents longer than 4,094 tokens change, so Gab, 100 subreddits and Twitter AAE are identical at both lengths, as expected. UncheatableEval is unchanged for all three models (its longest document is 4,082 tokens).

## Gemma: correction to the #8824 numbers

#8824's Gemma file gives Paloma macro 0.8494. Our lm-eval setup, which reproduces #8824's Qwen numbers, gives 0.8100 at 4k. The per-subset differences go both ways, so it is not a context-length effect:

| Paloma subset | #8824 | Ours, 4k | Ours, 32k |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Twitter AAE | 2.5644 | 2.0164 | 2.0164 |
| Gab | 1.4689 | 1.2869 | 1.2869 |
| 100 subreddits | 0.8904 | 0.8599 | 0.8599 |
| 4chan | 0.8415 | 0.8773 | 0.7979 |
| M2D2 S2ORC | 0.6173 | 0.6480 | 0.5861 |
| Penn Treebank | 0.8385 | 0.8932 | 0.8109 |
| **Macro (16)** | **0.8494** | **0.8100** | **0.7837** |

Short-document subsets are much worse in #8824 (Twitter AAE, Gab), while some long-document subsets are better in #8824 than in our 4k run (4chan, M2D2 S2ORC, Penn Treebank), which suggests a longer window there. The #8824 Gemma file is a summary without its lm-eval config, so we can't pin down the difference; BOS handling on short documents is one candidate. This issue now uses our own run for every Gemma number.

## Why earlier Marin numbers differ

Same checkpoint (step 156k), three ways of scoring Paloma:

| Scoring | Paloma split | Macro BPB |
|---|---|---:|
| In-training Levanter eval, 65,536-token packed sequences | val | 0.7896 |
| Levanter eval, 4,096-token packed sequences, full coverage | val | 0.8037 |
| lm-eval-exact (this issue) | test | 0.7812 |

- **Split:** lm-eval prefers a task's test split when it has one, and the Paloma template defines both. Levanter's validation sets use val. They are different documents (e.g. Falcon 1,553 val vs 1,711 test; mC4 1,108 vs 1,202).
- **Packing:** on UncheatableEval, where the documents are identical, the 4k packed eval gives 0.5395 and the exact method gives 0.5178. Packing cuts short documents at sequence boundaries and drops each subset's final partial sequence; lm-eval scores every document whole.
- **Context:** going from 65k to 4k packed sequences raised BPB most on long-document subsets (code +10.0%, M2D2 S2ORC +5.6%, RedPajama +5.1%) and barely moved Gab, Penn Treebank and Twitter AAE.

The Hero numbers and forecast in #8824 come from the packed Levanter eval on val, so they share this mismatch with the open-model rows there.

## Caveats

- `uncheatable_eval_hero`, the task #8824 used for Qwen, is not in evalchemy or the marin repo. Its per-subset document counts match ours exactly, but we could not confirm that it scores the raw `text` field.
- Training-data overlap with Paloma is unknown for both models. Paloma's C4, Dolma, RedPajama and Falcon subsets come from web-crawl sources close to our mix; the lead over Qwen is larger on Paloma (−7.0%) than on UncheatableEval (−1.3%).
- One evaluation per checkpoint. Scoring is deterministic, but the 262k vs 65k gap (−0.0017 Paloma, −0.0007 UncheatableEval) is small enough that we would not read much into it.
- Qwen's training compute is not public; #8824 assumes 36T tokens.

## Next

- Score Trinity Mini Base and Ling-lite-base-1.5 with the same lm-eval setup for more same-size base-model points. GPT-OSS-20B and GLM-4.7 Flash have no base checkpoints.
- Confirm the `uncheatable_eval_hero` task definition with the #8824 author.

comments.body:
🤖 **Multiple-choice evals: ours (step 156k) vs Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base and Gemma 4 26B-A4B**

All three models ran on the same setup: lm-eval 0.4.12, `local-completions` backend, `add_bos_token=True`, `max_length=4096`. Few-shot counts follow Open LLM Leaderboard v1, MMLU-Pro is the `leaderboard_mmlu_pro` multiple-choice variant, and no request was truncated.

| Task | Metric | Ours | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | Gemma 4 26B-A4B |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| MMLU, 5-shot | acc | 76.9 | **82.8** | 77.6 |
| MMLU-Pro, 5-shot | acc | 49.5 | **56.7** | 45.6 |
| ARC-Challenge, 25-shot | acc_norm | 67.7 | **73.9** | 73.6 |
| HellaSwag, 10-shot | acc_norm | 85.6 | 85.6 | **85.7** |
| WinoGrande, 5-shot | acc | 78.9 | 78.7 | **81.0** |
| PIQA, 0-shot | acc_norm | **83.7** | 82.5 | 83.6 |
| Mean | | 73.7 | **76.7** | 74.5 |

Standard errors: MMLU ±0.3, MMLU-Pro ±0.45, ARC-C ±1.3, HellaSwag ±0.35, WinoGrande ±1.1, PIQA ±0.9.

- **Commonsense (HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande):** we're level with Qwen. Gemma leads by 2.1 on WinoGrande.
- **Knowledge and reasoning:** Qwen leads by 6–7 points on MMLU, MMLU-Pro and ARC-C, even though our Paloma BPB is 7% lower than Qwen's (lower is better). The two measures disagree. *(Edited: this originally said Qwen led on Paloma, which was backwards.)* Against Gemma: +3.9 on MMLU-Pro, −0.7 on MMLU and −5.9 on ARC-C.
- **Caveat:** an MMLU of 76.9 is high for ~2B active parameters. Our mix includes Nemotron-CC v2 and other synthetic QA-style data, which may lift MMLU-format scores. Rescoring an earlier checkpoint would show whether the score jumped when the mix changed.

**How ours was scored:** grug checkpoints can't be served to lm-eval directly.
1. lm-eval recorded the exact token rows it would have sent (221k rows).
2. A v4-64 scored those rows from the step-156k checkpoint.
3. lm-eval replayed those scores so its own code computed acc and acc_norm.

A sha256 digest confirmed the replayed rows were identical to the scored ones. Qwen and Gemma were served with vLLM on 8×H100 (W&B `ul1rgzga` and `o5uiwrnr`).

Code (4273f050ce): `experiments/grug/moe/lm_eval_mcq_record_replay.py` and `experiments/grug/moe/eval_67b_a2b_lm_eval_mcq.py`.

🤖 **Full eval suite: Snowball-base vs. Marin 32B, Qwen3, Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4 (all base models)**

"Snowball-base" is the 262k-context checkpoint of this 67B-total / 2B-active model (step 157k). Full results page: https://claude.ai/artifact/Y5T3Y9MdZLcXCWc9JjMAxV

**Every comparison model is a base (pretrained) checkpoint. None is instruction-tuned.**

| Model | Checkpoint |
|---|---|
| Marin 32B | `marin-community/marin-32b-base` @ `f19b346` |
| Qwen3 | `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base` @ `1b75feb` |
| Qwen3.5 | `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base` @ `0f08130` |
| Gemma 4 | `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B` @ `24548b6` (the pretrained model; Gemma's tuned version is the separate `-it` repo) |

Every model uses the same lm-eval 0.4.12 setup: the `local-completions` backend, `add_bos_token=True`, `max_length=4096` and greedy generation. The open models were served with vLLM on 8×H100 with `--generation-config vllm`. Snowball-base was scored with the record/replay method from the previous comment.

## Scored the way the Marin 32B retro scored models

The retro reported a plain average, mean rank and mean reciprocal rank (MRR) over its task suite. The table below uses 17 of its 19 tasks at the retro's shot counts:
- WSC273 is left out because its dataset needs a loading script.
- GPQA is left out because it's gated and we don't have access.
- LSAT-AR runs 0-shot, because lm-eval 0.4.12 can't build AGIEval few-shot prompts.

Ranks are among these five models. Every number comes from our runs, not the retro's.

| Model | Active / total params | Training FLOPs (6·N·D) | Average ↑ | Mean rank ↓ | MRR ↑ | Tasks won |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5 | 3B / 35B | n/a | **73.7** | **2.06** | **0.69** | **9** |
| Qwen3 | 3.3B / 30B | ~7e23 | 70.9 | 3.12 | 0.41 | 2 |
| **Snowball-base** | 2B / 67B | ~1.2e23 | 70.9 | 3.24 | 0.36 | 1 |
| Gemma 4 | 4B / 26B | n/a | 67.9 | 3.06 | 0.44 | 3 |
| Marin 32B | 32B dense | ~1.2e24 | 67.7 | 3.24 | 0.45 | 4 |

## All results

| Task | Shots | Metric | Snowball-base | Marin 32B | Qwen3 | Qwen3.5 | Gemma 4 |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| MMLU | 5 | acc | 77.1 | 74.7 | 81.0 | **82.8** | 77.6 |
| MMLU-Pro | 5 | acc | 50.5 | 45.0 | **57.2** | 56.7 | 45.6 |
| ARC-Challenge | 25 | acc_norm | 67.5 | 66.8 | 67.3 | **73.9** | 73.6 |
| ARC-Challenge | 10 | acc_norm | 67.2 | 65.4 | 67.8 | **73.0** | 71.8 |
| ARC-Easy | 10 | acc_norm | 89.4 | 88.1 | 88.5 | 90.9 | **91.1** |
| OpenBookQA | 0 | acc_norm | **47.4** | 46.8 | 44.8 | 44.8 | **47.4** |
| BBH (multiple choice) | 3 | acc_norm | 59.0 | 59.7 | 60.2 | **69.0** | 55.4 |
| AGIEval LSAT-AR | 0 | acc_norm | 30.9 | 21.7 | 26.1 | **32.2** | 22.6 |
| GSM8K | 8 | strict match | 80.0 | 70.0 | 85.8 | **86.6** | 71.2 |
| MATH-500 | 4 | math-verify | 58.8 | 38.4 | **61.4** | **61.4** | 38.0 |
| HumanEval | 0 | pass@1 | 65.2 | 46.3 | 54.9 | **66.5** | 46.3 |
| WinoGrande | 5 | acc | 78.8 | **83.7** | 78.1 | 78.7 | 81.0 |
| WinoGrande | 0 | acc | 74.2 | **79.1** | 72.4 | 76.2 | 76.0 |
| CommonsenseQA | 10 | acc | 80.1 | 83.4 | 86.4 | **86.6** | 82.1 |
| COPA | 0 | acc | 91.0 | **93.0** | 89.0 | 91.0 | 92.0 |
| HellaSwag | 10 | acc_norm | 85.7 | **87.2** | 83.1 | 85.6 | 85.7 |
| HellaSwag | 0 | acc_norm | 83.1 | **85.0** | 81.4 | 83.7 | 83.2 |
| LAMBADA (OpenAI) | 0 | acc | 75.8 | 77.2 | 76.0 | 75.8 | **77.6** |
| BoolQ | 10 | acc | 87.7 | 89.2 | 88.3 | **90.0** | 87.9 |
| PIQA | 0 | acc_norm | 82.9 | 83.3 | 81.2 | 82.5 | **83.6** |
| PIQA | 10 | acc_norm | 85.4 | **85.9** | 82.9 | 84.8 | 85.8 |

## Bits per byte (lower is better)

These use the same lm-eval rolling-window method at 4096 tokens as the issue body.

| Eval | Snowball-base | Marin 32B | Qwen3 | Qwen3.5 | Gemma 4 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| UncheatableEval: Wikipedia English | 0.587 | 0.601 | 0.639 | 0.618 | **0.584** |
| UncheatableEval: GitHub Python | **0.248** | 0.322 | 0.260 | **0.248** | 0.256 |
| UncheatableEval: GitHub C++ | 0.260 | 0.324 | 0.250 | 0.247 | **0.243** |
| UncheatableEval: BBC News | 0.629 | 0.626 | 0.674 | 0.667 | **0.613** |
| UncheatableEval: arXiv Physics | 0.554 | 0.563 | 0.563 | **0.546** | 0.560 |
| UncheatableEval: arXiv CS | 0.544 | 0.562 | 0.563 | **0.539** | 0.553 |
| UncheatableEval: AO3 English | 0.799 | **0.787** | 0.816 | 0.808 | 0.788 |
| **UncheatableEval: mean of 7** | 0.517 | 0.541 | 0.538 | 0.525 | **0.514** |
| **Paloma macro (16 subsets, test split)** | 0.780 | **0.774** | 0.836 | 0.840 | 0.810 |

At 32k context, Qwen3's Paloma macro improves to 0.824 and its UncheatableEval is unchanged at 0.538.

## Takeaways

- **The 17-task average:**
  - Snowball-base ties Qwen3 (70.9) and is behind Qwen3.5 (73.7).
  - It is ahead of Gemma 4 (67.9) and Marin 32B (67.7).
  - On ranks it is at the bottom with Marin 32B (3.24 mean rank), because it is rarely first on any one task.
  - Its training compute is about 1/6 of Qwen3's and 1/10 of Marin 32B's.
- **Math and code are the biggest gains over Marin 32B:** +10.0 on GSM8K, +20.4 on MATH-500 and +18.9 on HumanEval. HumanEval is within 1.2 of Qwen3.5.
- **Marin 32B leads on commonsense and cloze tasks** (WinoGrande, HellaSwag, COPA, PIQA) and has the best Paloma macro. Snowball-base is close behind on Paloma (0.780 vs 0.774).
- **Knowledge-heavy multiple choice is where both Qwen models lead:**
  - MMLU: 77.1 vs 81.0 / 82.8.
  - MMLU-Pro: 50.5 vs 57.2 / 56.7.
  - BBH: 59.0 vs 69.0 for Qwen3.5.

Code: `experiments/grug/moe/lm_eval_record_replay.py`, `eval_67b_a2b_lm_eval_mcq.py` and `eval_67b_a2b_lm_eval_gen.py` (99056d1432, 14bec3f913).

issues.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
issues.body:
The hero GB200 canary timed out in Actions after 340 minutes without starting training. Kueue kept all 16 training tasks gated, while the monitor treated the child job's `RUNNING` state as proof that training had started and disabled its 18,000-second queue timeout. The metric report never ran. Classification: **infra/scheduling**.

Reproduce:
1. Submit a 16-task GB200 gang whose Kueue workload waits for admission. The child job becomes `RUNNING` while its tasks remain `BUILDING`.
2. In `scripts/ci/iris_monitor.py`, `_child_started` returns true for the child job's `RUNNING` state; `wait_for_child_job` drops the queue deadline. The Actions step then reaches its 340-minute timeout.

Expected: The queue deadline remains active until a training task starts. On expiry, the configured `shutdown` policy cancels the parent and reports a resource-exhaustion skip.

<details>
<summary>Evidence</summary>

- [Actions wait step](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/41692115065/job/126113066350) logged `Child ... reached RUNNING; dropping queue timeout` at 22:34:11 UTC and `The action 'Wait for hero canary' has timed out after 340 minutes` at 04:13:22 UTC.
- Iris task `/runner/hero-canary-41692115065-1-coord/grug-train-hero-canary-41692115065-1/0` remained `BUILDING`: `SchedulingGated ... Kueue workload iris-pg-f81e996a053a07ba-0: queue=cw-use08a-lq; waiting for Kueue admission`.
- Finelog `marin`, `iris.task_state`, root job `/runner/hero-canary-41692115065-1-coord`: all 679 samples from 22:34:46 to 04:13:36 UTC show `building=16`, `assigned=0`, `running=1` (the coordinator). The uploaded [diagnostics artifact](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/41692115065/artifacts/13294544130) has no training task output.
- The [monitor predicate](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8fd094fd23f0fd5b6992244c87f10a5bd99f49e3/scripts/ci/iris_monitor.py#L119-L123) reads only the child job state. A local call with child `RUNNING` and task counts `BUILDING=16`, `RUNNING=0` returns `True`.

</details>

## Canary run context

- Lane: `hero-gb200`
- Job ID: `/runner/hero-canary-41692115065-1-coord`
- GHA run: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/41692115065
- W&B run URL: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/hero-canary-41692115065-1 (training did not start)
- Date: 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-04 UTC

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 Memory sampling on the current `coord-memfix` instance isolates checkpoint-correlated retained RSS to writer tasks 0–127. Their median floor rose 11.7 GiB after the first save and 4.4 GiB after the second; tasks 128–175 stayed on the baseline slope. Each writer rank was assigned about 9.5–10.2 GiB, and `/proc` attributes the retained difference to anonymous memory across the four child Python processes.

The run contains #8609. The signature matches its documented persistent CUDA pinned-host BFC pool cost. The smaller second increment does not support projecting a fixed 30 GiB leak per save.

Incident record: https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/227

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body: 🤖 Correction after tracing the current checkpoint path: the long-lived `GlobalAsyncCheckpointManager` keeps the completed TensorStore commit futures in `_commit_futures`; `wait_until_finished()` joins but does not clear them, and the writes allow indefinite source-buffer references. This mechanism predates #8609 and plausibly retains one staged checkpoint share per writer rank. PR #8599 contained a reviewed post-join cleanup for these futures, but that part did not land with #8609. The pinned-host BFC pool in #8609 remains an additional allocator-level floor that clearing the manager cannot purge. Updated evidence and safe cleanup boundaries: https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/227

At 23:44Z the US-EAST-08A CoreWeave account reached 104.56 TiB against its 100 TiB quota, and CoreWeave suspended writes (`405 MethodNotAllowed: Account is write suspended for this availability zone`). Most of the 11.7 TiB rise since 20:26Z came from this deploy's forced checkpoints and durable handoff copies in `hero-checkpoints`.

Host memory stayed about 260 GiB below the limit. The cause is not confirmed; a storage-side stall left over from the suspension is the leading explanation. Training continued because checkpoint uploads run in background threads, but the next save would have blocked on it, so the task was preempted at 01:40Z (attempt 2, again from `step-146355`).

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
👋 I'm a new community contributor. Recently I audited the [Open-SWE](<https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Open-SWE-Traces>) part of the 10-05 SFT mix. Since [#10813](<https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10813>) proposes dropping failed and unknown traces, I only looked at successful traces (`resolved=1`, the agent's final patch passed the tests): all 49,925 of them in the two pinned `Qwen3.8-27B` partitions. 
🔗 Detailed Report with Examples: https://claude.ai/artifact/9vD2VkqXVPq5xNBA7Z1afp
Mainly there are 4 things:
1. 🚨 **[Incomplete prompt · may lead to hallucination]** NVIDIA's released prompts are missing a `"Solution Originality"` section that the teacher saw during generation ([NeMo-Skills template](<https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Skills/blob/592ebaec5a80e17a3535623d0f5704d29e13a64f/nemo_skills/prompt/config/eval/swe-bench/mini-swe-agent/swebench.yaml#L113-L127>)). In 32% of the traces, the CoT quotes rules from this section, even though those rules aren't in the released prompt. Training on this could teach the model to cite rules in its CoT that aren't in its prompt. We can easily add the section back to these traces.
2. ⚠️ **[Reward hacking]** A behavior that isn't in [#10788](<https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10788>) or [David's decision gallery](<https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/dlwh/snowball-sft-decision-gallery/2026.10.23/index.html>): guessing what the hidden tests check, or recalling the upstream fix from memory. In 61.5% of the traces, we found this in 3 or more turns (10 or more in 8.6%). In some traces, the agent writes its final code to fit its guess about the tests rather than the issue.
3. 🔍 **[Cheating risk]** In some sandboxes, a newer release of the same project, which already contains the fix, is installed in `site-packages` or left in a `build/` folder. For example, the task repo is `mkdocs-include-markdown-plugin` `2.8.0`, while `3.4.1` sits in `site-packages`. The agent finds it and diffs it against the repo, so the trace shows a model looking at the answer. It's rare (roughly 0.1–0.3% of traces), and in the cases we read, the agent says it won't copy it.
4. 🚧 **[Newer revisions]** [Newer NVIDIA revisions](<https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Open-SWE-Traces/commits/main>) add `Qwen3.8-27B` traces on more harnesses (OpenHands, SWE-agent, Claude Code, OpenCode) and traces from `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next`, which Marin doesn't use yet. I audited those too, and they'd need fixes first: in 8–18% of the `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` traces (depending on the revision), some turns carry reasoning text from a different conversation, and every OpenCode prompt ends with an extra `"`.

🙏 This is my first time contributing to Marin, so I'd appreciate a pointer on how best to hand this over. I've finished the audit and have per-trace results (which traces have which problems), but I'm not sure where they should go: upload them to HF as a dataset, open a PR that applies the fixes in the Open-SWE transform (maybe on top of [#10813](<https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10813>)), or something else?

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
The SWE-smith Harbor task packages in `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s` (and the same layout in `mlfoundations-dev/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests`) leave the repository's full git history in the agent's container. The image built from `environment/Dockerfile` keeps a local `main` branch with the unbroken code and about 944 other branches, so the agent can print the fix with `git diff HEAD main -- <package>` or `git show main:<file>`. `/tests` and `/solution` are correctly absent from the image.

Reproduce: build `swesmith-00003`'s `environment/Dockerfile` from the package, run it with no network, then `git log --oneline` (three commits: Initial commit, Bug Patch, Remove F2P Tests), `git branch -a` (944 branches including `main`), `git diff HEAD main -- oauthlib` (the exact fix).

Impact on existing data: in `open-athena/Kimi-2.5-swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s-maxeps-32k`, 860 of 5,237 passing trials (16.4%) and 433 of 4,119 failing trials run history-reading commands (`git show main:<path>`, diffs against `main` or `HEAD~N`, checkout or restore from history, `git log -p`). Some are benign (a diff against `HEAD~1` shows only the removed tests); many copy the original file. So the reported pass rate on these packages is inflated, and trace sets built on them carry shortcut solutions: the Kimi set above, the `GLM-4.7` and AgentTrove swesmith streams, and the allkimi relay data (`laion/calibforge-relay-traces`, `kimi_swesmith` rows) that was DARE-grafted into Snowball v0 (`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign3-DARE-Linear-02-2026.10.12`). SWE-bench Verified is not affected: there the fix is not in the repository's past.

A plain squash is not enough, because `tests/test.sh` itself uses history (`git checkout <task branch>; git checkout HEAD~1`) to restore the removed fail-to-pass tests before running pytest.

Expected: during the agent phase the repository has one commit, no other branches, no remote and no reflog; the verifier restores the fail-to-pass tests from outside the agent's view (for example, ship the test files in `tests/` and copy them in, or keep a git bundle that only the verifier unpacks). For each task, the gold patch still passes, the unpatched repository still fails, and the history-reading commands above return nothing.

Done when: a fixed package build exists with that validation on a sample of tasks, existing SWE-smith pass rates and training sets built on the leaky packages are re-reported with history-reading trials removed or flagged, and the shootout pool in #10213 uses the fixed packages.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The reported `swesmith-00003` image retains the pre-bug `main` branch and earlier commits, so an agent can recover the fix from Git history. Removing old refs alone is insufficient if the object database still contains the clean tree; the current verifier also uses `HEAD~1` to recover fail-to-pass tests. The reported 860/5,237 passing and 433/4,119 failing history-reading trials are contamination candidates, not yet an audited count of trials that copied the fix. Marin consumes these external packages and traces, while the package builder is outside this checkout.

**Relevant code and artifacts**
- [DCAgent package release](https://huggingface.co/datasets/DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s) — affected task source.
- [Shootout #10213](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10213) — waits for stripped packages.
- [AgentTrove ingestion](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/agenttrove.py#L17) — SWE-smith trace consumer.
- [Relay source PR #10027](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10027) — registers Kimi SWE-smith rows.

# Proposal

## Outcome

Publish an immutable, revision-pinned Harbor package release whose agent image contains the bugged working tree in one new Git repository with one commit, one task branch, no `main`/remote/tags/reflog, and no recoverable old objects. Keep the fail-to-pass test payload in Harbor's verifier-only `tests/` area and copy it into the repository when scoring. Record the old and new package revisions and per-task content digests; do not overwrite the release used by existing trials.

## Plan

1. Change the package producer to create a fresh `.git` after applying each bug patch, rather than squashing the existing repository in place. Export required test files from the source package into verifier-only storage before discarding history. Make `tests/test.sh` restore those files without `git checkout` or `HEAD~1`; keep `solution/` and `tests/` out of the agent container.
2. Validate a stratified sample across repositories and test layouts in offline Harbor runs. In each agent image, require one reachable commit and no old refs, remotes, reflogs, or dangling objects containing the clean fix. Exercise `git show main:<file>`, `git diff HEAD main -- <package>`, `git show HEAD~1`, `git log -p`, and `git fsck --unreachable`; none may reveal the clean file. For each sampled task, the untouched bugged tree must score 0 and the gold patch must score 1 under the revised verifier. Publish task IDs, package digests, commands, and results with the new release.
3. Audit the Kimi, GLM-4.7, AgentTrove, and allkimi relay/Snowball v0 provenance at trial or row level. Classify history commands as benign inspection, fix recovery, or unresolved; report raw and unflagged success rates with denominators, plus counts by outcome and category. Publish flagged row IDs or a reproducible manifest and clean-filtered trace revisions where the source can be republished. Annotate existing model and dataset results; filtering rows cannot undo training already performed on Snowball v0.
4. Pin the fixed package revision in the #10213 SWE-smith pool and block the eight-attempt generation until the package validation passes. Keep the already stated pilot-trace history filter separate from the new pool validation. Coordinate Harbor release acquisition with [#10198](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10198); its cache work does not repair the package contents.

## Risks and open questions

The package producer and release permissions are external to this repository, so the new dataset revision needs an owner with access to that build pipeline. The verifier payload must be checked against every sampled task's required test files; a one-commit image can still give false rewards if a file is omitted. Excluding all history-reading trials gives a conservative subset, not an unbiased replacement for a fresh evaluation on fixed packages.

comments.body:
🤖 A fresh GLM 5.3 trial on the raw package used the history to check its fix.

**Setup:** `swesmith-00003` from `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s` (revision 78b0d879), unchanged. Harbor at `marin-community/harbor@016dd78b`, mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 with a 32k context, Daytona sandbox, GLM 5.3 through the internal bulk service. The trial passed (reward 1, 16 model calls).

**History use in the trajectory:**
- Step 6: `git log --oneline -5 && git status` showed `Remove F2P Tests` / `Bug Patch` / `Initial commit`.
- Step 8: `git log --all --oneline -- oauthlib/oauth2/rfc8628/endpoints/device_authorization.py && git show 614b134:oauthlib/oauth2/rfc8628/endpoints/device_authorization.py`. The second command prints the pre-bug file (`614b134` is `Initial commit`).
- Step 17: `git diff 614b134 -- oauthlib/oauth2/rfc8628/endpoints/device_authorization.py && echo "IDENTICAL TO ORIGINAL"` printed `IDENTICAL TO ORIGINAL`. The agent confirmed that its edit matches the original file before submitting.

GLM made the edit itself at step 10, after reading the original file at step 8. So this pass is history-assisted, and a GLM pass rate on these packages would be inflated in the same way as the Kimi data.

**Visibility probe:** an oracle-agent probe printed the container state during the agent phase (no model calls).
- `/testbed`: 944 branches (`main`, the task branch, `remotes/origin/*` for every task), and `git log --all` lists every task's `Bug Patch` / `Remove F2P Tests` commits.
- `/tests`: absent.
- `/solution`: absent for model agents. Harbor uploads it only for the oracle agent.
- None of the other task files are present (`task.json`, `test_*_state.py`, `setup.sh`, `container.def`, `test_state.py`).

**Run folders:** `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/generation/dryrun/swe-dry3` (trajectory: `swesmith-00003__LQ7xGdF/attempts/000/agent/trajectory.json`) and `.../dryrun/visibility1`.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Fixed SWE-smith packages for the #10213 pool, with validation on 20 tasks. The same class of leak is also present in TMax.

**Fixed packages.** `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/pool/swesmith-packages.parquet` (sha256 `f004b109edf8aa9274693c07e01266d14469ec8c61fe695cc516aa1175117407`), 2,100 tasks. The schema is the same as the DCAgent parquet (`path`, `task_binary`), and the folder names are unchanged. The source is `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s@78b0d879`. The upstream dataset is not modified. Code: [`experiments/post_training/sft_shootout_pool/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/3bc613878c/experiments/post_training/sft_shootout_pool) on branch `task/206`.

- `environment/Dockerfile`: after the upstream `git fetch && git checkout <instance>`, the same `RUN` replaces the repository: `rm -rf .git && git init && git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main && git add -A && git commit -m "Initial commit" && git reflog expire --expire=now --all && git gc --prune=now`. This is a new `.git`, not a squash, so no old objects remain in the container's filesystem. The base image's lower layers still hold the old `.git`, but the container cannot read them.
- `tests/f2p_restore/`: the files that the upstream `git checkout HEAD~1` would change, at their parent contents, plus `deleted.txt`. They are computed from a bare clone of `github.com/swesmith/<repo>`. On `swesmith-00003` they match the image's own `git show HEAD~1:<path>` byte for byte.
- `tests/test.sh`: `git checkout <instance>; git checkout HEAD~1;` is replaced by `cp -a /tests/f2p_restore/files/. /testbed/` plus the deletions. The rest is unchanged. Harbor uploads `tests/` only to the verifier (checked in harbor 0.24.0 `verifier/verifier.py`; only `agents/oracle.py` uploads `solution/`).

**Validation** on 20 pool tasks, one from each of 20 repos, in local Docker following Harbor's phase order:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Agent-phase repository: 1 commit, 1 branch, 0 remotes, empty reflog, no `HEAD~1`/`main~1`/`origin/main`/`master` | 20/20 |
| Gold patch (`solution/solve.sh`) then `tests/test.sh`: reward 1 | 20/20 |
| Unpatched tree: reward 0 | 19/20 |
| Leak commands (`git log --all -p`, `git show HEAD~1`, `git diff HEAD main`, `git diff HEAD~1`, `git fsck --unreachable --lost-found`, `git stash list -p`, `git show main:<every file>`) print a clean-only line | 0/20 (upstream `swesmith-00003` control: 2/2) |

- `swesmith-01094` (`ariga/atlas`) also scores 1 unpatched with the unmodified upstream package, so its verifier does not detect the bug. This is an upstream defect, and it means DCAgent's "oracle verified" does not imply that an unpatched run fails.
- "Clean-only line": a source line the Bug Patch removed that occurs nowhere in the bugged tree. 7 of the 20 tasks have none, so only the ref checks apply to them.
- The filesystem search found no git leak. It did find copies of clean lines in installed packages: `setuptools/_vendor/typeguard` is an older vendored typeguard, which is relevant for `agronholm/typeguard` tasks (57 in the pool). The `_pytest` (iniconfig) and `rapidfuzz` (thefuzz) hits are probably coincidental.
- Residual: `github.com/swesmith/<repo>` is public and keeps every instance branch, so an agent with internet access can still fetch the fix. In the Kimi traces this happened once (`git fetch origin; git show origin/main:<file>`).

Per-task results: `pool/swesmith-validation-20.jsonl` and `pool/swesmith-leak-probe-20.jsonl`.

**TMax: same class of leak, different mechanism.** In `allenai/TMax-SFT-16.5K@848e2182` `tasks.zip`, 221 of 2,200 environments build verifier assets into the agent's image (for example `/opt/oracle/<reference program>`, `/app/verifier/ground_truth_valid_events.txt`, `/home/user/oracle.py`), and `test_final_state.py` reads them. In 181 of the 221, the instruction never names the path. In the #202 Qwen3.6-27B success traces (`allenai/tmax-sft`), 63 trajectories across 18 tasks name one of these hidden paths in a bash command. That is a heuristic: naming a path doesn't prove the answer was copied. The pool excludes the 181 (`excluded.jsonl`, `leak_risk=hidden_verifier_assets`) and keeps the 40 visible ones. TMax's Harbor converter (`hamishivi/tmax@6d3d606c`) does not copy `task.json` (including its `truth` field), `solutions/`, `setup.sh` or `test_initial_state.py`; `test_final_state.py` goes only to `tests/`.

**Effect on #202's pilot training set:** 860 Kimi history-reading passes and those 63 TMax trajectories were removed before training (manifest `selection.swesmith_git_history_rule` and `selection.tmax_hidden_asset_rule`).

🤖 The public `github.com/swesmith` mirrors are now unreachable while the agent runs, and a second leak was found in mini-swe-agent's own install.

**TL;DR**
- During the agent phase, the sandbox can reach only the model proxy. github.com, PyPI, apt and every other host fail DNS, and direct-IP HTTPS (GitHub 140.82.112.3, 140.82.114.4; 1.1.1.1) has its TLS handshake cut. Setup and the verifier keep full network.
- mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 installs a tool env that the agent can read. It holds clean copies of three pool repos: pygments, pandas, tenacity. GLM read `tenacity/retry.py` from it and called it "the reference". The conda base in the images also holds boltons 23.0.0. All four repos (469 tasks) are excluded from pool P.

**Why not a whole-trial block:** Harbor sets the Daytona network policy once per sandbox. Both the mini-swe-agent install and the SWE-smith verifier (`tests/test.sh`) download uv from github.com releases (`astral.sh/uv/0.7.13/install.sh`), so a whole-trial allow-list without github.com breaks them.

**Mechanism** ([`harbor_agents/trial_agents.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1555295d4d5a233e1bb854c814b927c21889574c/experiments/post_training/sft_shootout/harbor_agents/trial_agents.py), `AgentPhaseNetwork`, branch `task/207` @ `1555295d`): just before the agent's run, the live sandbox is switched to `domain_allow_list=iris.oa.dev` (the proxy host). The run starts once that host resolves, and the task's own policy is restored before the verifier. Each trial writes the applied policy to `agent/agent_network.json`, and the run's `driver_config.json` records it under `agent_network`.

**Measured** (null agent on swesmith-00008, -00698, -00763; HTTPS HEAD from inside the sandbox):

| Target | Before | Agent phase | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `https://github.com/swesmith` | 200 | DNS failure | 200 |
| `api.github.com`, `raw.githubusercontent.com`, `codeload.github.com` | 200 | DNS failure | 200 |
| `https://140.82.112.3/`, `https://140.82.114.4/` (GitHub by IP) | 200 | TLS handshake cut | 200 |
| `https://1.1.1.1/` | 403 | TLS handshake cut | 403 |
| `pypi.org`, `deb.debian.org`, `archive.ubuntu.com`, `www.google.com` | 200 | DNS failure | 200 |

On these unchanged trees the verifier completed afterwards and scored 0, as expected. With GLM (`swe-net2`), 3/3 trials passed under the limit, and all 76 proxy calls returned 200. In one trial GLM ran `pip install pytest ...` and saw `No internet`.

**Tool-env leak:** in `swe-net2/swesmith-00763` (jd/tenacity), GLM ran `sed -n '136,175p' /root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/tenacity/retry.py`. A probe ran mini-swe-agent's real setup on one task from each of the 36 repos (`toolenv2`). It found the same 80 distributions on every image. Only three of them are pool repos: pygments (222 tasks), pandas (196) and tenacity (30). Every conda-based image also ships conda's own `boltons-23.0.0` under `/opt/miniconda3/pkgs`, including the mahmoud/boltons image (21 tasks). The install is now pinned (`mini-swe-agent-2.1.0-constraints.txt`, sha256 `c67d1ee2…`, Python 3.12), so this set cannot drift between the pilot and the full run. SWE-smith ingestion also drops any trace whose commands or outputs touch `/root/.local/share/uv/tools/`.

**Run folders** (`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/generation/dryrun/`):
- `netprobe2`, `netprobe3`, `netprobe4`: network probes; `agent/network_probe.json` per trial.
- `swe-net2`: GLM trials under the limit.
- `toolenv2`: tool-env listing; union in `tool_env.json`.

Data point for Open-SWE, which is in the 10-05 SFT mix but not in the list above. I checked the successful traces (`resolved == 1`) of the two pinned Qwen3.8-27B mini-swe-agent partitions of `nvidia/Open-SWE-Traces` (revision `f967cba3`, 49,925 traces) for lines of the fix that show up in command output before the agent writes them.

**Rule.** A trace is flagged when at least 3 lines added by the reference patch (30+ characters, not imports or comments, not in the removed lines or the prompt) first appear in the output of a command that reads git history (`git log/show/diff`), `site-packages`, `node_modules`, `build/`, `dist/` or `.egg-info`, or the network (`curl`, `wget`, `pip download`, URLs), before the agent writes them. I then read 5 flagged traces per channel.

| Channel | Flagged | Read | Confirmed leak |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| git history | 153 | 5 | 0 |
| `site-packages` | 104 | 5 | 3 |
| `node_modules` | 83 | 5 | 0 |
| other (`build/lib`, network, …) | 29 | 5 | 1 |

- **Git history:** no case like the SWE-smith one. The git hits I read were the agent's own checkout or edits, or an older commit unrelated to the fix.
- **A newer release of the task's own package is installed in the image.** This is a different path from the mini-swe-agent tool env above: the system `site-packages` (`/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages`) holds a newer release of the package being fixed, and that release already contains the fix. The fourth case is a stale `build/lib/` copy inside the repo (oauthenticator). In all four, the agent found the copy (for example, diffed it against `/testbed`) and said it would not copy it; I did not check whether it used it anyway.

issues.author: ravwojdyla-agent
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Fuzzy verification in PR #8114 filters a broad set of duplicate candidates after connected-component clustering. This experiment measures whether removed documents are duplicates, whether retained candidates are missed duplicates or distinct documents, and whether the containment and unique-trigram limits should change. A small canary suggests that the current rules are precise but conservative. The 4K smoke and full-text review are in progress.

## Description

The audit reads full text from the CoreWeave source data and writes private reports to GCS. It samples removed, retained, boundary, random, source, length, score, and cluster-size strata. Corpus text stays in private artifacts.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Review at least 500 complete document comparisons, measure the quality of current decisions, test counterfactual parameter settings, and recommend either the current verifier or a measured parameter change. Run matched and larger samples after the 4K output passes its integrity checks.

## Status

The current 4K smoke contains 2,783 candidate clusters and 5,628 documents from 3,998 source shards. It uses 128 shuffle partitions and 32 workers. At 2026-08-11 18:44 UTC, stage 0 was complete and the verification stage was at 2/128 tasks. All 32 workers were alive after 14 preemptions, with no application error.

The exploratory canary has 47 reviewed candidate decisions:

- The current rules removed 4 candidates. All 4 appeared safe to remove.
- The rules retained 43 candidates. Manual review marked 28 as safe removal opportunities and 15 as unsafe to remove.
- The current rules found 4 of the 32 reviewed safe removal opportunities.
- A counterfactual containment limit of 0.90 with 8 unique trigrams found 7 safe removals and no unsafe removal. Limits of 0.85/8 and 0.80/8 found more safe removals but also 1 and 2 unsafe removals, respectively.

The canary is small and selected for inspection, so it does not support a production parameter change by itself. The production defaults have not changed.

A separate stress set contains 1,018 hard pairs from issue #6854. The current rule accepted three pairs, and all three were safe removals. A much smaller relaxation to 0.99 containment with 2 unique trigrams added 20 removals; directional review marked 16 safe and 4 unsafe because they lost a schedule month, a quote ending, an attribution, or a signature. This stress result is evidence against a global threshold reduction, including the canary-fitted 0.90/8 setting.

## Links

* Logbook: will be linked when the research branch is published
* W&B Report: none
* Important updates:
  * [PR #8114](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8114)
  * [4K V6 smoke](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Frav%2Ffuzzy-verification-audit-4k-v6-20260811)

## Decision Log

- 2026-08-11: Bound the smoke shuffle at 128 partitions after an unbounded run created 3,998 downstream verification tasks.
- 2026-08-11: Set the smoke store-ready and recovery limits to 7,200 seconds after a 1,800-second deadline expired during worker recovery. This did not change production defaults.
- 2026-08-11: Defer parameter changes until the 4K integrity checks, stratified review, matched treatment, and larger samples are complete.

## Conclusion

Open. The final report requires at least three days of analysis and at least 500 complete document comparisons.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 Manual text review is complete for all 266 document decisions in the 250-cluster smoke.

- Removed by verification: 107 of 109 were safe removals. Two kept a lower-quality representative; neither lost unique information.
- Kept by verification: 80 of 157 looked safe to remove, while 72 would lose information and 5 would keep lower-quality text.
- Pair types across both decisions: 105 contained copies, 19 format-only copies, 97 near duplicates, 31 same-template pairs with different facts, and 14 related but non-duplicate pairs.

This result supports the current high-precision boundary. A broad threshold reduction is not safe: 49.0% of the reviewed kept documents would lose information or quality if removed. issues.author: ravwojdyla-agent
issues.body:
`_select_duplicates` discards the first record of each id group and emits only the rest, so `_write_shard` writes `{id, dup_doc: True}` for each duplicate and nothing for the occurrence that survives (experiments/datakit/global_exact_dedup.py:150, experiments/datakit/global_exact_dedup.py:160). The attributes are sparse by design: on the full 292-source run only 59 sources produced any attribute directory. Nothing in the output records where a flagged duplicate's canonical lives.

Tracing one flagged id therefore costs a scan. Establishing that the four duplicates in `cp/uk_hansard` were cross-source required reading the `id` column of all 11 files in that source, and naming the source that holds each canonical requires a further full pass per candidate source, over sources that can hold thousands of files. The canonical is already well defined at the point it is dropped: the lowest `(file_idx, row_index)` over sources sorted by name, which the reducer holds when it calls `next(records)`.

Done when:
- each duplicate row carries the canonical's location, as the global `file_idx` and `row_index` or the equivalent source tag plus file and row index
- a flagged duplicate can be traced to its canonical without scanning a source
- consumers of the current `{id, dup_doc}` schema either keep working or are updated together with the schema

issues.author: mcwitt
issues.body:
## Summary

On the `moe_hero_fsdp` GB200 config, `token_embed` **and both of its Adam moments** are fully replicated on every device. That is **8.81 GiB per GPU — 89% of the entire per-device train state (9.87 GiB)** — for a parameter that is 2.94 GiB.

Replicating the *parameter* is deliberate and documented (`experiments/grug/moe_hero_fsdp/model.py:61-64`):

```python
# The embedding is fully replicated for a local lookup. The language-model head
# is replicated across racks and FSDP-sharded within each rack.
_EMBED_PARTITION_SPEC = P(None, None)
_LM_HEAD_PARTITION_SPEC = P("data", "model")
```

**The optimizer moments inheriting that spec looks unintended.** The locality argument justifies replicating the weight — `_embedding_gather` (`model.py:95`) does a local lookup with no collective. It does not justify replicating `mu` and `nu`, which are touched only by the optimizer update and never gathered per token.

## Measurement

Instrumented dump of the initialized train state, 1 rack (64 GPUs), `d6144 / E128 top-4 / vocab 128256`, `num_layers=1` (minimal-repro config from #7344), `offload_opt_state=True`:

```
[statemem] leaves=90 per_device_total=9.87 GiB global_total=73.22 GiB ratio=7.4x

dev=2.936 GiB glob=2.936 GiB .params.token_embed                                    spec=P(None, None)
dev=2.936 GiB glob=2.936 GiB .opt_state...inner_states['adam'].inner_state[0].mu.token_embed  spec=P(None, None)
dev=2.936 GiB glob=2.936 GiB .opt_state...inner_states['adam'].inner_state[0].nu.token_embed  spec=P(None, None)
```

For contrast, `output_proj` — the same 128256 × 6144 shape — is sharded and costs 64× less per device:

```
dev=0.046 GiB glob=2.936 GiB .params.output_proj                                    spec=P('data', 'model')
dev=0.046 GiB glob=2.936 GiB .opt_state...inner_states['adamh'].inner_state[0].mu.output_proj
dev=0.046 GiB glob=2.936 GiB .opt_state...inner_states['adamh'].inner_state[0].nu.output_proj
```

So the LM head and the embedding are the same size, and one costs 0.14 GiB/device across param+moments while the other costs 8.81 GiB.

## Why it matters now

Sharding `mu`/`nu` over `data` (64-way) while leaving the weight replicated would recover **~5.8 GiB per GPU** and leave the lookup path untouched.

That is not a rounding error on this config. In #7344 we are chasing allocation failures on GPUs reporting **~18 GiB free of 186 GiB**, where a large transient fails with `cuMemAllocAsync ... CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY`. 5.8 GiB is roughly a third of the remaining headroom. It is not the root cause there — the failing allocation is a step transient, not persistent state — but it is a third of the margin the run has to absorb one.

## Suggested fix

Give the embedding's optimizer state its own spec rather than inheriting `_EMBED_PARTITION_SPEC`, e.g. shard `mu`/`nu` on `P("data", None)`. Worth checking whether the MuonH/AdamH grouping (`inner_states['adam']` vs `['adamh']` vs `['muonh']`) makes this a per-group setting.

Two things to verify before/after:
- the embedding update is numerically unchanged (moments are elementwise; sharding them should be a pure placement change),
- no new collective appears in the update — if resharding the moments introduces an all-gather per step, the trade may not be worth it.

## Repro

The dump comes from a small instrumentation helper that walks `jax.tree_util.tree_leaves_with_path(state)` and reports `sharding.shard_shape(...)`-derived per-device bytes per leaf. Happy to upstream it behind a flag if useful — `GrugTrainerConfig.sharding_dump_path` already writes a sharding artifact, but it records specs without sizes, so the cost of a replicated leaf is not visible from it.

🤖 Filed while investigating #7344.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
## Correction: the HBM figures above are conditional on `offload_opt_state=False`

I need to correct the headline number in this issue. The measurement was real but I
mislabelled what it measures.

**The probe reports logical sharded bytes, not HBM residency.** It walks
`tree_leaves_with_path(state)` and derives per-device bytes from `sharding.shard_shape()` —
it never reads `memory_kind`.

Under the hero default `offload_opt_state=True`, the optimizer moments are placed on
`pinned_host` at initialization and copied device-ward per step immediately before
`optimizer.update`, then returned to pinned host
(`experiments/grug/moe_hero_fsdp/train.py:557` and `:637`).

So of the three replicated 2.936 GiB `token_embed` leaves I reported, **only the parameter
is HBM-resident in the steady state**; the two moments are host-resident between steps.

Corrected claim:

- ❌ "8.81 GiB per GPU — 89% of the per-device train state — with ~5.8 GiB recoverable" as a
  statement about **default** HBM. That figure holds only for `offload_opt_state=False`, or
  transiently during the optimizer update.
- ✅ The **logical replication is real**: `token_embed` and both moments are `P(None, None)`
  while the identically-shaped `output_proj` is `P("data", "model")`, a 64× per-device
  difference in the sharded case.

I also want to flag a cost I understated: sharding the moments while keeping the weight
replicated is **not free**. The optimizer would then need an explicit sharded-update or
re-replication strategy, or moment communication. That trade needs measuring, not assuming.

This remains a worthwhile independent memory optimization — it is simply **not** evidence
for #7344, and I should not have leaned on it there. The connection I drew to allocation
headroom in that issue is withdrawn.

Thanks to an independent review pass for catching the `memory_kind` omission.

issues.title: [grug] token_embed optimizer moments are replicated, costing ~5.8 GiB/GPU of avoidable HBM

issues.author: yonromai
issues.body:
## Summary This issue defines the repeatable GB200 inference benchmark used to evaluate GrugMoE architecture choices before the hero pretraining run. It fixes the validation anchor, hardware, closed-loop rollout workload, plateau throughput metric, repeat rules, and artifact gates so architecture comparisons change one model property or declared bundle at a time. Experiment 0 validated the rolling benchmark with R3 on, but also showed the frozen experiment R3 carrier is expensive: 302.5347 generated tok/s/GPU with R3 off versus 225.6882 with R3 on (-25.40%). The primary architecture matrix should therefore run with R3 off, while production-like chat R3 is measured separately on the reference, payload-changing candidates, and finalists. The companion tracker #7913 is the execution checklist; this issue is the protocol. ### Helpful links - [Companion architecture tracker #7913](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7913) - [Experiment 0 R3 protocol update](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7912#issuecomment-5185894476) - [Reviewed preflight findings](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12b4a6f0d8a1ef1e4021e1fa5b0ba0893fb087ed/notes/preflight/findings.md) - [Merged validation-anchor PR #7820](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7820) > [!IMPORTANT] > This issue freezes the inference benchmark, not the pretraining architecture. > The modeling team still owns quality constraints, exact candidate configs, > and the final model. Lower precision, other inference engines, general vLLM > tuning, and speculative decoding are out of scope. ## Benchmark at a glance | Item | Fixed rule | | --- | --- | | Hardware | Four `gb200-4x` nodes: 16 GB200 GPUs in one NVLink domain | | Primary topology | `PP1 TP1 DP16 EP16`; only the topology experiment varies it | | Model | The tracker's exact `d6144`, 48-layer, top-4-of-128 validation anchor | | Stack | Marin's vLLM fork; prefix caching, chunked prefill, CUDA graphs, sampled-token logprob, fixed output length, ignore EOS, and separate R3 routed-expert controls | | Weights / precision | Seeded vLLM dummy weights; BF16 weights and KV cache | | Comparison | Change one model property or declared bundle; keep the commits, flags, workload, seed, routing fixture, and measurement code fixed within the pair | | Headline | Generated tokens/s/GPU during an unprofiled stable plateau | | Material change | At least 5%, with paired repeats agreeing and the delta larger than paired variation | ## Workload Use a rolling, closed-loop queue. A completed request is replaced immediately, which matches saturated rollout generation better than an external-arrival server benchmark. | Cohort | Cached history | User/tool append | Generate | Final context | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Short | 10,240 | 1,024 | 2,048 | 13,312 | | Medium | 30,720 | 1,024 | 2,048 | 33,792 | | Long | 62,464 | 1,024 | 2,048 | 65,536 | Give each cohort one third of the live slots. For the reference, attention/KV finalists, any memory-cliff candidate, and the final model, also run four sequential 2,048-token response turns per branch. Carry each answer into the next prefix. This produces 8,192 generated tokens and final contexts of 22,528, 43,008, and 65,536 tokens. Run a separate one-turn 131K capacity stress for the reference and attention/KV finalists. Preserve earlier thinking blocks in the append-only history by default. If the post-training renderer strips them, freeze that behavior instead and recalibrate the reference. Do not benchmark both policies in the main matrix. ## Run and repeat rules 1. Calibrate concurrency and `max_num_batched_tokens` once on the R3-off reference. Choose the lowest concurrency within 5% of the best observed point, then freeze all runtime flags. Recalibrate only for the topology comparison. 2. Before any architecture comparison, pass two identical rolling R3-off reference arms. Measure R3 separately on the reference using the production-like chat contract and on candidates that change payload shape or transport behavior. The A/A arms must differ by at most 2% and show normal health. 3. Each ordinary arm must include at least 120 plateau seconds, 250,000 generated tokens, and one full workload-manifest pass. All three floors must pass. 4. Compare candidates as A/B and B/A in separate same-allocation pairs. Add a third pair only if the first two disagree, straddle 5%, or show abnormal health. 5. Confirm a decision-driving irreversible choice once on a fresh allocation. 6. Collect headline throughput without a profiler. Profile only an unexplained regression of at least 5%, a missing expected gain, or a health anomaly. If the two-minute A/A fails, extend both arms to five minutes, then ten minutes only if needed. A candidate may receive one labeled tuned diagnostic after a cliff or surprising result; it never replaces the fixed-setting result. ## Valid result gate A result is valid only when all applicable checks pass: - [ ] In-flight requests stay at or above 95% of target concurrency throughout the measured plateau; ramp and drain are excluded. - [ ] Every request succeeds, every required branch completes, and client and engine token totals reconcile. - [ ] The primary comparison has zero KV preemptions and no unlisted setting change. - [ ] When R3 is enabled, it contains every expected token/layer/top-K expert ID with correct alignment. - [ ] MoE-geometry and EP-topology pairs include both canonical dummy routing and one deterministic balanced-routing control. - [ ] Any new hot-path implementation family has one no-op throughput control. - [ ] Exact configs, train-to-serve parity, commits, image, placement, workload, and artifact readback are recorded. Serving must compute every selected top-K expert contribution with the frozen QB bias. No inference capacity factor may drop assignments. ## Execution checklist - [ ] Modeling acknowledges the validation anchor and marks every live P1 candidate **Include** or **Exclude**, supplying one complete config for each included candidate. - [ ] Check whether vLLM's closed-loop dispatcher accepts the frozen workload. Reuse it when it does; otherwise port only its scheduling and steady-window logic into the existing preflight harness. - [ ] Freeze clean, pushed Marin and Marin-vLLM commits, image, flags, workload, history policy, R3 carrier, route fixture, and artifact schema. - [ ] Use the preflight's zero-retry unattended Iris gang path for calibration, A/A, and candidate pairs. - [ ] Pass the rolling R3-off A/A gate and the separate reference production-like chat-R3 measurement. - [ ] Run the companion tracker's order and attach one valid result packet to each completed row. - [ ] Share the inference recommendation with modeling before architecture freeze. Keep experimental code on long-lived Marin and Marin-vLLM branches. Open a PR only for code with a clear reusable consumer or for the selected production model path.
Exact load generation and plateau calculation Use six frozen roots per cohort and eight rollout branches per root. A completion is replaced by the next request from that cohort's frozen root/branch schedule, with no think time. Keep each root and its branches on one DP rank. Freeze and hash token IDs, root and branch order, turns, sampling parameters, and per-request seeds. Warm with disjoint requests, reset the prefix cache, then populate histories through normal server requests. For the four-turn trajectory, use these exact initial histories: | Cohort | Initial history | Total generated | Final context | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Short | 10,240 | 8,192 | 22,528 | | Medium | 30,720 | 8,192 | 43,008 | | Long | 53,248 | 8,192 | 65,536 | The separate 131K stress uses 121,856 cached tokens, a 1,024-token append, an 8,192-token response, and `max_model_len=131072`. Open the plateau when in-flight requests reach `ceil(0.95 × target_concurrency)`. If any sample falls below that threshold, discard the window and reopen it after recovery. Close the plateau while the queue is still full, after all duration, token, and manifest floors pass. Then stop refilling and exclude the drain. ```text generated tokens/s/GPU = sum of unique vLLM generation-counter deltas during the plateau / plateau seconds / serving GPUs ``` Use generation-counter snapshots at plateau boundaries. Do not reconstruct plateau throughput from completed requests. After drain, cross-check the whole-run counter delta against successful-request token totals. The smaller-local-KV stretch may use only 8,192- and 65,536-token final contexts, with the same append and generation lengths. Add no midpoint or 131K arm to that first screen.
Routing, R3, profiling, and implementation controls Record per-expert and contiguous EP-rank assignment histograms for every arm. Canonical dummy routing is primary. Because preflight found it highly skewed, repeat MoE-geometry and EP-topology pairs with one deterministic balanced runtime route. Use that control elsewhere only when a decision-relevant delta coincides with different route loads. Do not add skew or capacity-factor sweeps. Pin the vLLM commit and R3 carrier. Run the primary architecture matrix with R3 off. At the reference point, report the production-like chat-R3 throughput delta, payload bytes, and transport time. Add R3-on controls for candidates that change payload dimensions or transport behavior, and for decision-driving finalists; its cost need not be linear across architectures. For a new hot path, compare the implementation enabled versus a no-op path once at the reference configuration. Profile a triggered anomaly for only a few seconds at the same saturated point and link it to the unprofiled result.
Metrics and saved artifacts Each result reports: | Group | Required fields | | --- | --- | | Throughput | Generated and processed-prompt tok/s/GPU; paired delta; plateau seconds and generated tokens | | Load / latency | Target and min/mean/max in-flight; successes/failures; cohort completions; server p50/p99 TTFT and TPOT; client end-to-end latency | | KV / scheduler | Predicted semantic KV bytes; active bytes/live sequence; reserved and peak pool bytes; resident sequences/DP rank; prefix-hit ratio; running/waiting requests; preemptions | | MoE / R3 | Per-expert and per-rank assignments; max/mean rank load; route fixture; carrier; payload bytes; transport time; ID alignment | | Reproduction | Immutable Marin and vLLM URLs; image digest; lock; flags; workload hash/seed; Iris job; task count; NVLink domain; artifact prefix | Keep predicted semantic KV bytes, physically active pages, and the reserved reusable pool separate. Explain an active-versus-predicted gap above 10%. Store each run under: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/romain/inference-bench/grugmoe-architecture///` ```text manifest.json events.jsonl metrics/raw-*.prom metrics/map.json result.json result.md profiles/ # diagnostic runs only ``` The manifest includes code, image, dependency, config, workload, job, placement, flags, R3, and final-prefix provenance. A separate authorized task must read every claimed object, verify hashes and aggregates, and exit successfully.
What preflight proved—and did not prove The [reviewed preflight](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12b4a6f0d8a1ef1e4021e1fa5b0ba0893fb087ed/notes/preflight/findings.md) proved that the exact anchor starts and generates on four `gb200-4x` nodes with `PP1 TP1 DP16 EP16`. Exact-path parity, prefix reuse, active-KV accounting, P0 implementation smokes, unattended launch, and independent artifact readback passed. Its drained-wave A/A arms produced 1,578.25 and 1,583.50 aggregate generated tok/s, a 0.3324% difference, with zero preemptions. This proves feasibility and drained-wave repeatability. It does not pass the rolling A/A gate or rank an architecture. The dummy router left 121 of 128 experts unused, and the bounded Snowball attempt failed before model load, so this is not trained-model performance evidence. | Provenance | Frozen value | | --- | --- | | Live Marin / vLLM | [`a3320a3`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/a3320a3043018ee923bc98bf2e6e6eef3f03a6fe) / [`2c2bef3`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/commit/2c2bef33dfbd7aef3c9d4433a7e4110f77d56a4a) | | Reviewed heads | [`12b4a6f`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/12b4a6f0d8a1ef1e4021e1fa5b0ba0893fb087ed) / [`73b6fc9`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/commit/73b6fc9cc20c2712ec8798dd017d8a5bc9f55b5b) | | Image | `ghcr.io/marin-community/iris-task@sha256:5e2a69af91a000cb999e6ff0d92933874bd3142eb45469fc64fc7a3f5db64fbb` | | Placement | Four whole GB200 nodes in `DH1-129-US-EAST-08A`; `PP1 TP1 DP16 EP16` |
References - [#7201: GB200 architecture TPS tracker](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7201) - [#7673: provisional pretraining and RL timelines](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7673) - [#7706: serving topology study](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7706) - [#7164: train-to-serve routing parity](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7164) - [#7248: R3 payload and transport measurements](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7248) - [#7820: exact merged GrugMoE reference](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7820)

comments.body:
> [!IMPORTANT] > **Protocol update from Experiment 0:** use **R3 off** for the primary > architecture matrix. Measure the production-like R3 path separately on the > reference, on candidates that change its payload shape or transport behavior, > and on decision-driving finalists. Experiment 0 passed its frozen rolling R3-on A/A gate: **221.0431 versus 223.6248 generated tok/s/GPU**, a **1.1612%** symmetric difference with no request failures or KV preemptions. It therefore validates the rolling instrument under that carrier. The matched carrier check also showed that R3 can materially affect the measurement: **302.5347 tok/s/GPU off versus 225.6882 on (-25.40%)**. The tested carrier is deliberately heavier than the current RL path: it returns routing for prompt plus generated tokens from `/v1/completions` as a base64 NPY payload, while MarinSkyRL consumes generated-token-only routing from `/v1/chat/completions`. The 25.40% result is therefore a measured cost for this frozen experiment carrier, **not** an estimate of production MarinSkyRL cost. Until the issue body is reconciled, this comment supersedes its instructions to calibrate with R3 on and keep R3 on throughout the primary matrix. The next gate is R3-off calibration and A/A, plus one matched control using the actual MarinSkyRL chat-R3 contract. Architecture comparisons may follow immediately in the same execution goal once that gate passes.
