issues.author: mcwitt
issues.body:
A production-band 16-node GB200 gang on `cw-us-east-08a` has sat `SchedulingGated` for over an hour behind two batch-band 8-node jobs, because Kueue only enters preemption on quota pressure and the gang is blocked by rack topology while the fleet still has free GPUs. This is the residual of #8781: #8782 made accelerator quota binding at fleet size (`max_slices: 216`), which fixes the fleet-full case but not the rack-full case, and on a 12-rack NVL72 cluster the rack is the unit that matters.

## Observed

`/mwittmann/ra2a-8870-whl3-wh-coord/grug-train-ra2a-8870-whl3-wh` (production, 16 × gb200-4x, coscheduled on `multinode-nvlink-ib`), submitted 2026-09-04T21:17Z. Every task `building` with:

```
Kueue workload iris-pg-4b06617fd63a6fdf-0: queue=cw-use08a-lq; QuotaReserved (Pending): couldn't assign flavors to pod set e4c4e2ba: topology "multinode-nvlink-ib" allows to fit only 2 out of 16 pod(s). Total nodes: 207; excluded: resource "cpu": 192, resource "memory": 1
```

Occupancy at the time (`job_config.priority_band` from the controller DB): the hero at system on 176 nodes (11 racks × 16), and three 8-node jobs on the remainder — `/zack/exp157-rope-delta-l2-controlmatch-r5-east08-gb200-driver` **batch**, `/zack/exp177-aug-contact-order-ce-gb200-r96-driver` **batch**, `/zack/exp177-soft-target-cw-r103-…-driver` whose GPU child is production. Preempting either batch job would free 8 nodes on its rack; together with the rack's existing free nodes that is the 16 the gang needs. Kueue never evaluates it.

## Why

`ClusterQueue.preemption.withinClusterQueue: LowerPriority` is set (`lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/kueue_manifests.py:374`), and the design note at `:109-113` states the intent: binding accelerator quota exists "so Kueue can check whether removing lower-priority victims creates a compatible accelerator placement." But quota is derived from `max_slices` — the whole reserved fleet — so it binds only when every GPU in the cluster is allocated. With ~7 free nodes scattered across racks the workload is quota-Fit, reaches TAS, fails on topology, and is downgraded to NoFit without victim selection. Exactly the mechanism #8781 documented, one level up: fleet-level quota cannot express rack-level pressure.

The preemption events Iris *has* recorded on this cluster are from the Kubernetes scheduler (`default-scheduler: preempting to accommodate a higher priority pod`), which acts on pod priority after Kueue admission. A gang that never clears the Kueue gate never reaches it, so the system band does not help either.

## Consequence

Band semantics are inverted for the workloads the bands exist for. Any gang whose size is a rack fraction larger than the free space on the best rack queues indefinitely behind batch work, at production or system priority, while the cluster reports free capacity. On this cluster that is every EP64 job (16 of a rack's 18 nodes) whenever any other job holds more than 2 nodes on each non-hero rack.

## Possible directions

- Quota per topology domain rather than per fleet, so rack-level pressure is visible to victim selection; Kueue's TAS preemption work (kubernetes-sigs/kueue, "TAS-aware preemption") is the upstream track and #8781's install script already flags it as version-sensitive.
- Failing that, an Iris-side reclaim: when a coscheduled workload above batch reports TAS lack-of-fit for longer than a threshold, evict enough lower-band pods on the best-fitting rack to make it fit. Crude, but it restores the contract.
- At minimum, surface it: a gang gated on topology lack-of-fit with lower-band victims available should say so in `task describe`, rather than looking like ordinary queueing.

Related: #8781 (fleet-level fix, #8782), #7916 (same shape for CPU reservations on rno2a), #8247 (domain-blind placement stranding GPUs).

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

### Research

This is unintended, and the current Kueue policy cannot enforce the documented Iris band contract for topology-only pressure. Kueue defines `withinClusterQueue: LowerPriority` only for an incoming Workload that exceeds unused nominal quota; Iris enables that policy in [`build_cluster_queue`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/28d310aea26e0f44237949833652f2706a89204c/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/kueue_manifests.py#L342-L377), but [`accelerator_nominal_quotas`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/28d310aea26e0f44237949833652f2706a89204c/infra/pulumi/src/iac/coreweave/kueue.py#L46-L59) derives one fleet-wide quota from 216 physical GB200 nodes. East08's topology model guarantees only 16 schedulable nodes in each 18-node rack ([`SCHEDULABLE_RACK_NODES`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/28d310aea26e0f44237949833652f2706a89204c/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/coreweave_topology.py#L27-L50)), so a 16-node Workload can be quota-Fit and then TAS-NoFit; Kueue skips victim selection in that state.

The upstream preemption API documents quota pressure as the eligibility condition, and topology-aware priority handling remains open in [kubernetes-sigs/kueue#9992](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/issues/9992). No open Marin PR overlaps this issue.

### Proposed Fix

The smallest correct fix is topology-aware victim selection in Kueue: when a higher-priority Workload changes from quota-Fit to TAS-NoFit, evaluate lower-priority Workloads as victims and admit it when their removal creates a valid topology assignment. After upstream support exists, update Iris's Kueue pin and extend [`gpu_gang_smoke.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/28d310aea26e0f44237949833652f2706a89204c/lib/iris/tests/e2e/gpu_gang_smoke.py) with the East08 shape: two batch 8-node gangs fragment a rack, then a production 16-node gang reclaims them.

Reducing the global quota to 16/18 of physical capacity is not a correct substitute. It permanently withholds capacity that smaller workloads can use, can evict work on unrelated racks, and still cannot express which victims free a compatible domain. An Iris-side evictor would duplicate Kueue's workload lifecycle and topology snapshot; I do not recommend adding that race-prone second scheduler.

comments.author: mcwitt-agent
comments.body:
🤖 Closing on behalf of @mcwitt: the mechanism this issue describes is wrong, so there is nothing to fix here. [Discussion in Slack](https://openathena.slack.com/archives/C0AHF5KV11Q/p1793808199495639?thread_ts=1793754103.865239).

**Kueue does preempt on topology pressure.** When a workload fits quota but fails topology placement, Kueue [switches it to `Preempt`](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/blob/v0.18.3/pkg/scheduler/flavorassigner/flavorassigner.go#L733-L761) and [checks each candidate victim set with a topology fit](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/blob/v0.18.3/pkg/scheduler/preemption/preemption.go#L623-L634). It returns `NoFit` only if the workload would not fit on an empty cluster. This code is in v0.18.0 onward and the logic is unchanged through v0.20.4, so it applied to the v0.18.3 deployed when this issue was filed. The earlier comment's reference to kubernetes-sigs/kueue#9992 is also off target: that issue covers pods outside Kueue's accounting, not victim selection. #7806 recorded the behavior on `cw-us-east-08a`: a 16-replica interactive gang showed `Pending the preemption of 8 workload(s)`, then was admitted.

**Scheduler test against v0.18.3.** These are simplified, single-cycle scheduler tests with CPU as the only resource, not a live cluster run. The pending workload is a production job that needs 16 nodes on one rack.

| Cluster state | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 12 racks of 18 nodes, one interactive node on each | Admitted without preemption |
| 12 racks of 16 nodes, one interactive node on each | Preempts 1 interactive job |
| 12 racks of 18 nodes, 3 interactive nodes on each | Preempts 1 interactive job |
| Spare rack with 8 batch + 8 batch nodes, 2 free | Preempts both batch jobs |
| Spare rack with 8 batch + 8 production nodes, 2 free | No preemption, since it would free only 10 of 16 |

**Likely explanation of the original report (inferred; rack placement was not verified).** The Kueue message said the best rack could fit only 2 of 16 pods, so preempting one 8-node batch job would leave 10 free, not the 16 this issue states. One of the three 8-node jobs was running at production while the dashboard showed interactive (#8928). If it shared the spare rack with a batch job, no permitted preemption could have made room.

A gang can still wait while lower-priority jobs start if preempting every lower-priority job would not make room, for example when a rack is short of nodes. #8928 remains open. Clearer reporting of why a gang is gated would still help, since the same `QuotaReserved (Pending)` message appears whether or not preemption can help.

issues.title: [iris] Production gang queues behind batch jobs on Kueue TAS lack-of-fit when the fleet, but not the rack, has free GPUs

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Base models that don't stop at their end-of-turn token go on to write a fake user turn. We made three base models write that turn on purpose, across 122 conversations, to see who they imagine on the other side. Write-up with charts and examples: [The users base models imagine](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/benjaminfeuer/the-users-base-models-imagine/2026.11.04/index.html).

- **Realism.** The Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and Marin 67B A2B Snowball bases write users that look like real WildChat follow-ups on length, lowercase use and question rate. Qwen3.5's imagined users average 34 words, 25% are all lowercase and 38% are questions. For WildChat the figures are 46 words, 25% and 40%.
  - Part of that realism is copying: in 41% of Qwen3.5's turns, more than 30% of the text comes from earlier in the conversation.
  - Qwen3-30B-A3B's "users" run long and incoherent; 60% hit the 384-token cap.
- **Register.** The imagined user takes on the earlier user's register. After a casual request, 73% of Qwen3.5's imagined users write all lowercase; after a formal one, none do.
- **Tone.** The imagined user is cooperative: it follows up on the task or starts a new one. Wrong assistant answers draw essentially no complaints, and none of 161 hand-coded turns was hostile.
- **Leaks.** Run past their natural stop, the models write a user turn at very different rates: Snowball 36% [31–40], Qwen3.5 10% [6–13], Qwen3-30B 0.2%. Leaks concentrate in agentic and chitchat conversations.
- **Credential-shaped strings.** In two spontaneous generations, Snowball base wrote five strings shaped like API credentials.
  - The four `hf_` strings are the wrong length for real Hugging Face tokens.
  - One `sk-` key matches a real provider format, so it can't be ruled out.
  - None of the five appears in GitHub code search, and none was tested against a service.
  - The open follow-up is to search Snowball's pretraining mix for the exact strings.

## Description

**Elicitation.**
- *Forced mode:* each conversation ends with a complete assistant turn. We append the model's own user-turn opener, as rendered by its chat template and asserted, then sample until its end-of-turn token.
- *Spontaneous mode:* we leave the last assistant turn open and sample with `ignore_eos` until end-of-text. Any user turn the model writes after its own turn ends is parsed out as a leak.
- *Sampling:* temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0, 4 seeded samples plus 1 greedy per conversation and mode.
- *Scale:* 3,660 generations on vLLM, on Iris cw-rno2a, about 7.5 H100-hours.

**Conversations.** The 122 conversations cover nine situations:
- IFBench prompts, each answered once by a strong author and once by a weak author;
- everyday requests written by hand, some as casual/formal pairs;
- math and code, each with a right and a wrong answer;
- agentic tool use;
- users that are visibly another AI;
- chitchat;
- assistant refusals;
- the same request under four system personas.

**Analysis.**
- Automatic features on every turn.
- 162 forced turns hand-coded for intent, tone and apparent author. The codebook was written before coding started. The coder was the analysis agent, a language model, working alone, so there is no inter-coder reliability.
- Reference features computed from 500 WildChat second-turn user messages and from the 100 IFBench prompts.
- Cluster-bootstrap 95% CIs over conversations.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Find out which users each base model's pretraining has taught it to expect, and how the context shapes them. The factors tested are:
- benchmark versus everyday versus agentic conversations;
- right versus wrong assistant answers;
- the earlier user's register;
- the system persona.

## Status

Complete. One follow-up is open: check whether any credential-shaped string occurs verbatim in Snowball's pretraining mix.

## Links

* Write-up: https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/benjaminfeuer/the-users-base-models-imagine/2026.11.04/index.html
* Code (context builder, sampler, features, contrasts, codebook): https://gist.github.com/penfever/00b99c4634c89c30d733ffc9cc9bcd7c
* Raw generations, contexts and hand codes: https://gist.github.com/penfever/bcb1b5c4879390ad2f81aa28d1eb243e
  * Emails and phone numbers are redacted.
  * The five credential-shaped strings are masked: only the first 4 and last 2 characters show.
* Iris jobs: `/benfeuer/hu-full-{qwen35-base,qwen3-base,snowball-base}` on cw-rno2a.

## Decision Log

- Kept each chat template's real rendering, including Qwen3.5's empty `<think>` blocks on earlier assistant turns. Snowball's opener ends in a single newline, as its template renders it.
- Spontaneous mode uses `ignore_eos`. The Qwen3.5 base mirror has no generation config, so vLLM otherwise stops at its turn-end token. The leak rates therefore describe what models write after their natural stop, not production serving.
- Skipped the optional LLM classifier, so only the 162 hand-coded turns have intent and author labels.
- Masked the credential-shaped strings rather than removing them, so their format stays visible without making them usable.

## Conclusion

All three base models imagine a cooperative person who continues the session and doesn't check the assistant's answer. For Qwen3.5 and Snowball, that person also copies the conversation's register and looks like a real chat user on the surface. Snowball leaks a user turn far more often than the Qwen bases, in every situation. Why the pretraining mixes produce these users is not established here; testing it would take mix ablations.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body: 🤖 Triage: The experiment is complete; the remaining credential-origin check is a separate data audit. The public generations mask all five strings, so the audit first needs the unredacted values from the experiment owner or access-controlled run outputs and the versioned pretraining corpus manifest for the Snowball checkpoint. Search the identified corpus shards for exact matches within their storage region, then report hit counts and source identifiers without publishing the strings or copying the corpus. A match would establish corpus presence, not that the model copied that occurrence; zero matches would be limited by the completeness of the corpus manifest. No repository change or PR is indicated by the completed experiment.

issues.title: [eval] What users do base models hallucinate past their end-of-turn token?

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
We believe that formal verification is essential for open source models to get better at math, and better generally! Lean, a popular formal verification language primarily used for mathematical proofs, is one of the most popular avenues for this kind of improvement. We don't have RL data we trust for Lean, nor do we have evals we trust. Marin needs both in order to continue improving in this domain.

cc @Robertboy18

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

Marin already grades Nemotron RLVR1 Lean responses with a pinned Lean 4.12/Mathlib compiler ([#10080](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10080), [#10088](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10088)). That establishes a reward path for those rows, but not an audited training corpus or held-out theorem-proving eval. [#10214](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10214) excluded Lean from its mixed RLVR runs because Iris task pods could not start the Docker task machine; the [current eval policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197) lists no Lean proof benchmark.

**Relevant code**
- [lean_grade.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/nemotron_ultra/lean_grade.py) — current compiler-backed reward.
- [lean.Dockerfile](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/nemotron_ultra/lean.Dockerfile) — pinned toolchain and Mathlib.
- [lean_compiler.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/lean_compiler.py) — task-local execution path.
- [proofpile.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/datasets/proofpile.py) — existing pretraining corpus to check for overlap.

# Proposed Fix

1. **Freeze the eval first.** Inventory candidate Lean problem sets and record licenses, source revisions, theorem IDs, proof provenance, and required toolchains. Create public development and sealed test manifests; check statement/proof overlap against RLVR1, Proof-Pile 2, and proposed training sources. Specify prompts, token and time budgets, pass@1/pass@k, and how compiler failures and missing scores enter the denominator. Done when pinned reruns reproduce the same task IDs and verdicts.
2. **Audit the verifier.** Reuse the compiler path with controls for invalid proofs, `sorry`/`admit`, changed statements, extra axioms, and timeouts. Review a stratified sample of accepted and rejected attempts independently, publish disagreement counts, and resolve reward exploits before training. Keep the compiler and Mathlib revision identical between data validation and eval.
3. **Curate RL tasks.** Normalize licensed Lean statements and headers into provenance-bearing task records, deduplicate by theorem and near-duplicate text, and compile reference proofs where provided. Keep eval problems and their proof variants out of training. Resolve the Iris task-pod execution gap seen in #10214, then run a real task-session smoke test. Done when each released row has a source, toolchain pin, verification outcome, and contamination decision.
4. **Measure transfer.** Run pinned baseline models on the frozen eval, reporting pass@1/pass@k with uncertainty, per-source scores, and compiler/error rates. Compare a small Lean RL pilot against its starting checkpoint on the same eval and publish the dataset and run revisions. Expand the data or training budget only if the audited reward and held-out scores support it.

issues.author: muchanem
issues.body:
Taskforge decides whether a build error is the program's (it costs a revision and goes back to the author) or the host's (the workpiece is held and retried) by walking the exception chain. This issue proposes replacing that heuristic with a rule: an error is authored unless it is a typed infrastructure cause that the SDK raised.

### Current behaviour

`stage40_build_with_program/infrastructure.py` classifies in three steps:
- `infrastructure_failure` searches the chain for a typed host link (`BuildInfrastructureFailure`, `ModelUnavailable`, an `httpx` error).
- `authored_failure` then treats an error as the program's only if each root link is one of a fixed set of programming-error types (`TypeError`, `ValueError`, `LookupError`, ...) whose innermost frame lies in the program's files.
- Anything else becomes `BuildInfrastructureFailure("unclassified_build_failure")`, which holds the workpiece and retries it.

The heuristic runs at the step site and the group site (`run.py`), at `build_process.build_result`, and in the coordinator.

It has failed in two measured ways:
1. **Author-owned errors held as infrastructure.** In acceptance-measure wave 1, 15 of 96 workpieces were abandoned after four identical retries on errors the author owned and could have fixed. A `RuntimeError` raised in the program's own step body, or `json.loads` on the program's own string, is held this way. Before 03d0e09b61, both cost a revision.
2. **Explicit `BuildFailure`s lost** (found by forklady42 on #10298). `authored_failure` skipped any link with a `__cause__`, so a `BuildFailure` raised `from` a library error became `unclassified_build_failure` after the `TaskGroup`. This affected the SDK's own `grade_candidate` and `publish_image` failures, and lost the failure's step. #10298 fixes this one case in ad327f072e: a `BuildFailure` is now authored wherever it sits in the chain. Case 1 is unchanged.

### Proposed rule

- A build error is authored unless it is a typed infrastructure cause raised by the SDK.
- `BuildInfrastructureFailure.cause` becomes that closed `InfrastructureCause` enum instead of a `str`, so pyrefly can check it.
  - The free-form labels in use today join the enum or are retired: `unclassified_build_failure`, `model_request_unavailable`, `web_unavailable`, `author_incomplete`, `empty_answer_ungraded`, `candidate_*`.
  - The enum moves below `infrastructure.py` to break the import cycle with `context.py`: into `context.py`, or into `taskforge/sandbox/host_failures.py`, which already holds the host classifiers and sits below both stages.
- The three raise sites in `taskforge/agentic/tools.py` (`grading_unavailable`, `grading_interrupted`, `validation_incomplete`) are Rav's agentic path and need coordinating with him.
- One classifier replaces the copies at the step site, the group site, `build_result` and the coordinator.

### Drawback

A real infrastructure fault that nobody has typed would reach the author as the program's error, spending revisions on something the author cannot fix, until it is typed at the SDK boundary. Today such a fault is held instead.

### Status

This is parked for Mark's decision after the staged stack (#10297, #10298, #10300, #10301) lands. Related review threads: #10298, on `BuildInfrastructureFailure.cause` typing and on the classification precedence.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

The current #10298 branch still converts unrecognized build exceptions into `unclassified_build_failure` at the step, `TaskGroup`, child-result, and agentic-author boundaries. `BuildInfrastructureFailure.cause` and the child-process `HostFailed.cause` are strings, so new labels can bypass the intended taxonomy. The prerequisite stack (#10297, #10298, #10300, #10301) is open; #10298 already owns these files, and I found no separate fix PR for #10920.

**Relevant code**
- [`infrastructure.py#L175-L245`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ad327f072eccbb04b74aa4330680b4af22b3deae/lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/stage40_build_with_program/infrastructure.py#L175-L245) — whitelist and chain classification
- [`run.py#L266-L326`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ad327f072eccbb04b74aa4330680b4af22b3deae/lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/stage40_build_with_program/run.py#L266-L326) — step and group fallbacks
- [`build_process.py#L369-L386`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ad327f072eccbb04b74aa4330680b4af22b3deae/lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/stage40_build_with_program/build_process.py#L369-L386) — child-result classification
- [`agentic_author.py#L654-L679`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ad327f072eccbb04b74aa4330680b4af22b3deae/lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/stage40_build_with_program/agentic_author.py#L654-L679) — author-session classification
- [`coordinator.py#L440-L481`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ad327f072eccbb04b74aa4330680b4af22b3deae/lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/stage_coordinator/coordinator.py#L440-L481) — revision versus hold

# Proposed Fix

After the staged stack lands and Mark accepts authored-by-default ownership, make one follow-up PR with `Fixes #10920`:

1. Move `InfrastructureCause` beside `BuildInfrastructureFailure` in `context.py`; type its `cause` and the serialized `HostFailed.cause` as that enum. Inventory every free-form raise in the SDK, agentic author, and [Rav's three agentic-tool sites](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ad327f072eccbb04b74aa4330680b4af22b3deae/lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/agentic/tools.py#L419-L518). Add genuine host causes to the enum and retire `unclassified_build_failure`; coordinate the agentic-tool changes with Rav.
2. Convert model, HTTP, machine, and store failures to typed causes where the SDK owns the call. A raw `httpx` exception anywhere in authored code must not acquire infrastructure ownership merely because of its Python type. Preserve the exception chain so a typed host cause wins over an authored error in a mixed `ExceptionGroup`.
3. Use one classifier at the step, group, child-result, author-session, and coordinator boundaries: typed SDK infrastructure cause holds; other build exceptions carry their original traceback and step into `BUILD_FAILED` and consume a revision. Keep the child result and coordinator retry policy consistent with that decision.
4. Add regressions for a step raising `RuntimeError`, `json.loads` failing on the program's string, `BuildFailure` raised from another error, mixed authored/typed-host groups, and the child-result round trip. Check that typed host failures hold and authored failures revise. Run the Taskforge suite, pyrefly, pre-commit, and the pre-PR lint review.

Decision needed before implementation: should `BuildExpired` remain a separate hold outcome, and which store failures should hold without retry? Both currently bypass authored classification. The default-authored rule needs an explicit answer for those paths so it does not turn host faults into spent revisions.

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
Add small structural evals for basic agent behavior. The [BixBench trace audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6300963037) found answers left in chat instead of the required file, and simulated tool execution with no actual tool calls. The audit does not isolate model behavior from serving, tool parsing, or harness behavior.

Cover four checks:

- Required-file submission: when instructed to write an answer to a path, verify that a nonempty file exists in the actual task environment. An answer in chat or a claimed write does not pass.
- Actual tool execution: verify a real tool invocation and its execution status for tasks that need one. Tool-call markup, invented tool responses, or a narrated shell session do not pass. Distinguish missing/invalid invocations, executor failures/timeouts, and successful execution.
- Thinking disabled: verify the emitted response respects the supported `thinking=false` setting. Define the prohibited reasoning-channel output or delimiters under the pinned template; this checks observable output, not internal reasoning. Keep extraction/serving errors distinguishable from model violations.
- URL loading: when a task explicitly requires information at a supplied URL and a retrieval tool is available, verify an actual retrieval attempt. Record tool/network failures separately from failure to attempt retrieval.

Done when:

- Each check has minimal tasks and positive/negative grader fixtures, including narrated execution and missing-file cases.
- Results separate protocol compliance, submission completeness, and answer correctness. Passing the structural check alone must not imply a correct answer.
- Traces retain the request settings, raw response, parsed tool calls, execution events, and checked artifacts needed to locate failures.

Scope is evaluation additions; training interventions are separate.

Related: #10060 (output-contract validation), #10061 (tool-protocol syntax and localized supervision).

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The [BixBench audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6300963037) found 156/205 tasks without the required answer file and a trace that narrated shell execution with no tool event; the evidence does not isolate model output from parsing or execution. Harbor keeps a trajectory but maps verifier reward to one `correct` value, leaving no separate protocol, submission, and answer labels. The duplicate preflight found no PR for these four checks; [#10045](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10045) covers BFCL training and syntax diagnostics.

**Relevant code**
- [`trial_driver.py#L316-L352`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/trial_driver.py#L316-L352) — validates one Harbor dataset and agent.
- [`runner.py#L126-L145`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py#L126-L145) — reads trial result and trajectory path.
- [`runner.py#L172-L189`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py#L172-L189) — equates reward with `correct`.
- [`eval.py#L111-L141`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/finestore/src/finestore/eval.py#L111-L141) — sample and metric contract.
- [`eval.py#L288-L342`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/finestore/src/finestore/eval.py#L288-L342) — flattened trajectory fields.

# Design: agent protocol probes

Add a versioned four-task diagnostic through the evaluation launcher. Pin the model revision, chat template, tool schema/parser, agent/runtime revision, request settings, and task content. Use Harbor's existing local dataset path for sandbox checks; use a dedicated single-turn request to the same served endpoint for `thinking=false`, so the grader can inspect the exact request and response independently of an agent's final message.

1. **Required file.** Ask for a short known answer in `/workspace/answer.txt`. The verifier reads that path in the task environment after the agent stops and records existence, byte count, and content hash. Score file presence separately from matching the known answer; chat text or a claimed write cannot satisfy presence.
2. **Tool execution.** Ask the agent to obtain a per-trial nonce with an exposed shell tool. Record the raw generated response before tool parsing, parsed calls, dispatch/start/end events, and exit status. Label missing or invalid invocation, executor error/timeout, and successful execution separately. A narrated shell session, tool-call markup in ordinary text, or invented tool response must fail the execution check.
3. **Thinking disabled.** Send `enable_thinking=false` only for a pinned template that supports it. Define forbidden reasoning fields and template delimiters for that template; inspect the raw HTTP response and parsed message. An unsupported setting, server error, or extraction failure gets its own status, never a model-violation label. This measures emitted output only.
4. **URL loading.** Supply a task-local HTTP URL serving a per-trial nonce and make a retrieval tool available. Score a request observed by that endpoint or an executor-recorded retrieval attempt. Record no attempt, retrieval/network failure, and successful retrieval separately; compare the answer to the nonce independently. The local endpoint avoids public-site availability as a source of false failures.

Store one versioned evidence bundle per trial with request settings, raw response, parsed calls, execution events, URL access log, and checked file metadata. Archive it alongside the existing raw trajectory through `EvaluationStore`; link it from the sample's grading detail. Export `protocol_compliance`, `submission_completeness`, and `answer_correctness` as distinct numeric metrics; keep `not_evaluable` and its reason in grading detail when a prerequisite failed. Keep `EvalSample.correct` for answer correctness when assessed, and report each rate with its denominator; a structural pass alone cannot raise answer accuracy.

## Validation

Write grader fixtures before implementation. Include positive cases for all four checks: file submission, executed tool call, no emitted reasoning, and successful URL retrieval. Negative cases cover missing and empty files; answer only in chat; a fully narrated fake tool transcript; malformed call; dispatch failure and timeout; URL answer without retrieval and retrieval failure; reasoning-field and delimiter leaks; and a serving/extraction error. Assert both the label and the retained evidence for every fixture. Run the checked-in Harbor config through preflight and one capped end-to-end diagnostic suite covering all four checks on the pinned reference setup before using model comparisons. Keep [#10060](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10060) and [#10061](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10061) separate: they cover general output contracts and tool-call syntax/training.

## Open question

Do the pinned Pi/Harbor/vLLM versions expose the pre-parser generated text and executor lifecycle? The current archive records parsed tool calls and observations, but does not establish those boundaries. If either is unavailable, add capture there before grading that failure class, and mark earlier traces `not_evaluable`.

comments.author: davidlundgren
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The [design comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10393#issuecomment-6302257478) covers the cause: Harbor maps verifier reward to a single `correct`, and ATIF trajectories record parsed tool calls and observations but no executor lifecycle or pre-parser text. No open PR covers these checks.

- [`runner.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3ae74d9560/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py) — one reward per trial.
- [`trajectory.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3ae74d9560/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/trajectory.py) — the trajectory archive the evidence bundle sits beside.
- [`eval.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3ae74d9560/lib/finestore/src/finestore/eval.py) — `EvalSample`, `Grading.detail`, and `EvaluationStore.add_artifact`.

# Proposed Fix

This PR adds the grader layer in `marin.evaluation.protocol_probes`: a versioned evidence bundle, one typed spec and grader per check, the four minimal tasks, archiving that stores the bundle and links it from the sample, and denominator-aware rates for `protocol_compliance`, `submission_completeness`, and `answer_correctness`. Fixtures cover every positive and negative case listed in the design. When a prerequisite is missing, such as no captured executor lifecycle, the result is `not_evaluable` and never a model violation. A follow-up will connect the tasks to Harbor runs and the served endpoint once the capture question is settled.

comments.author: davidlundgren
comments.body:
🤖 Snowball v0.1 (`open-athena/Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1`) on the same probes, served by vLLM on one 8xH100 node through SkyRL's evaluation-only entrypoint (`protocol_probes_eval.py` in #10399), 8 minutes wall once the model is staged. All 32 probes graded:

- `tool_execution`: `executed` 8/8, answer wrong 8/8. `url_loading`: `retrieved` 8/8, answer wrong 8/8. The model calls the tool, then keeps generating past `<|eot_id|>` and writes its own `<tool_response>` before the real result arrives, and answers from the fabricated one. The dumped rows show the fabricated output; the real tool ran.
- `required_file`: `submitted` and correct 3/8, `missing_file` 5/8. Several misses are malformed call markup (`<tool_call name="shell">` … `</tool_name>`), which the parser rejects.

By contrast Qwen3-0.6B never calls a tool (`no_invocation`, `not_attempted`, `missing_file` on all 24 tool, URL and file probes). The model's `generation_config` lists both `<|end_of_text|>` and `<|eot_id|>` as EOS; whether the continuation past `<|eot_id|>` is a serving stop-token setting or the model is the next thing to check.

comments.author: davidlundgren
comments.body:
🤖 Correction to my previous comment on Snowball v0.1: the tool turns in those traces were the real observations the harness fed back, not fabricated output. The raw response text in the dump interleaves model turns with observations, which misled the first reading. Each dumped row now also carries the parsed `messages` the grader read.

Those messages exposed a serving-client bug: Snowball's tokenizer names `<|end_of_text|>` as EOS while its template ends turns with `<|eot_id|>`, so the client left `<|eot_id|>` on every graded reply and the exact-match grader scored right answers 0 on multi-turn probes. The client now strips whichever special token the server stopped at (#10399, `7b81a5e760`). Rerun on one 8xH100 node (8 minutes, 32 probes):

- `tool_execution`: `executed` 7/8, correct 3; `not_executed` 1. `url_loading`: `retrieved` 8/8, correct 4. The wrong answers wrap the nonce in prose ("The token is …") where the probe asked for the value alone.
- `required_file`: `submitted` and correct 2/8, `missing_file` 6/8, several with malformed call markup the parser rejects.
- `thinking_disabled` (every row, thinking off): `respected` 27/32, `reasoning_emitted` 5/32.

Average probe score 0.53, against 0.19 before the fix. Qwen3-0.6B, which never calls a tool, is unaffected because `<|im_end|>` is its EOS.

issues.author: raspberryice
issues.body:
> Context: 
> I've been running some IF training experiments on my own and noticed that that Nemotron RLVR1 blend checker has issues and the model is prone to reward hacking such as producing non-sense answers or language switching to circumvent constraints. Since the same dataset was used in Snowball RL training, I'm reporting the issue here to raise awareness about IF training set quality issues. 


_Some instruction-following (IF) rows in the Nemotron RLVR1 blend reward answers that ignore the request (all caps, Title Case, no Latin letters, or a non-Latin script), score at random, or cannot be passed._ 

[Cleaned-v3](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Nemotron-RL-Ultra-RLVR1-Cleaned-v3-2026-09-30) has 1,142 such rows among its 11,817 IF rows. Cleaned-v3 is the training set of the Antidoom RLVR1 v2 run, which produced Antidoom RLVR1 Step12, and of its Reference-KL continuation, which produced Reference-KL Step20 (#9735). The PivotRL mixed-RLVR arms (#10214) also train with its IF rows in the mix (#10215). Snowball v0.1 (Smartie run `.32`, #10305) trained on no IF constraint rows, but it started from the Campaign 2 merge, whose parents include Antidoom Step12 and Reference-KL Step20 (#9975).

| Constraint | Rows | Prompt text | NVIDIA checker |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `count:lowercase_counting` | 869 | "all lowercase words should appear at most N times", N = 2 or 3 | Allows at most N lowercase words in the whole answer, so only all-caps, Title Case or non-Latin answers pass ([instructions.py:2348](https://github.com/abukharin-nv/verifiable-instructions/blob/f46a5ac87b1400a4f8973039844b6be9b56e3faf/verifiable_instructions/instructions.py#L2348)) |
| `letters:letter_counting` with `relation: "less than"` | 203 | "Answer with less than N letters", N = 2 or 3 | Passes only answers with fewer than N Latin letters, such as `42` ([instructions.py:2355](https://github.com/abukharin-nv/verifiable-instructions/blob/f46a5ac87b1400a4f8973039844b6be9b56e3faf/verifiable_instructions/instructions.py#L2355)) |
| `length_constraints:nth_paragraph_first_word` with `nth_paragraph = num_paragraphs + 1` | 77 | "There should be 3 paragraphs. ... Paragraph 4 must start with word feedback." | Replaces the out-of-range `nth_paragraph` with `randint(1, num_paragraphs + 1)` on every call, so the paragraph it checks is random ([instructions.py:929](https://github.com/abukharin-nv/verifiable-instructions/blob/f46a5ac87b1400a4f8973039844b6be9b56e3faf/verifiable_instructions/instructions.py#L929)) |
| `count:counting_composition` | 1 | "delimited by the markdown divider: * * *" | Splits paragraphs only on `***`, so an answer that uses the prompt's `* * *` divider fails ([instructions.py:2440](https://github.com/abukharin-nv/verifiable-instructions/blob/f46a5ac87b1400a4f8973039844b6be9b56e3faf/verifiable_instructions/instructions.py#L2440)) |

Eight rows carry two of these constraints.

Antidoom RLVR1 v2 and Reference-KL graded IF rows with MarinSkyRL's [`grade_instruction_following`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/53bb00e83910a7dbd3f21efcb1c9384231b0fca3/skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/envs/nemotron_ultra/instruction_following.py#L61-L84). It runs NVIDIA's pinned `verifiable_instructions@f46a5ac` checks and returns 1.0 only when every constraint passes. Its paragraph patch ([L54-L57](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/53bb00e83910a7dbd3f21efcb1c9384231b0fca3/skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/envs/nemotron_ultra/instruction_following.py#L54-L57)) applies only when `nth_paragraph` is missing, and the 77 rows set it. MarinSkyRL's opt-in verifyit path rejects those 77 rows at preparation ([instruction_verifyit.py:242](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/3a8e8a72681011012ebb59c0c1ed34688ad6fdea/skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/envs/instruction_verifyit.py#L242)). It is off by default ([env.py:80](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/53bb00e83910a7dbd3f21efcb1c9384231b0fca3/skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/envs/nemotron_ultra/env.py#L80)), and I found no setting that enables it in the Antidoom RLVR1 v2 run notes or the Reference-KL config. The reward does not check that the answer addresses the request. It also does not check the answer's language, so a non-Latin answer passes `lowercase_counting` on an English prompt. 3,166 of the 11,817 IF prompts (26.8%) contain CJK characters.

The task-curation grader on main (#10077) checks these constraints with verifyit, then asks a GLM-5.3 judge whether the answer addresses the request ([graders.py:316-378](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/nemotron_ultra/graders.py#L316-L378)). verifyit's `count:lowercase_counting` passes answers with at least N lowercase words ([ifeval.py:547-552](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/ifeval.py#L547-L552)), which inverts the prompt. Its `nth_paragraph_first_word` check fails every answer to the 77 off-by-one rows ([ifeval.py:143-155](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/ifeval.py#L143-L155)), so a run trained on this grader gives every sample on those rows reward 0. The GLM-5.3 judge scores the 203 `letter_counting` rows instead of a letter count.

11,688 of the 11,817 Cleaned-v3 IF rows appear verbatim in [`nvidia/Nemotron-Cascade-2-RL-data`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-Cascade-2-RL-data) `IF-RL/train.jsonl`. 

**Our observations:** 
In a GRPO run of Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 on that file, scored with open-instruct's IFEvalG checkers (whose `lowercase_counting` rule matches NVIDIA's), the `lowercase_counting` pass rate rose from 0.21 at step 0 to 0.96 at step 199. From step 79 on, 85–93% of those passes were mostly CJK (more than 20% CJK characters). Mostly-Chinese answers to English IFEval prompts went from 0% at step 0 to 34.5% at step 199, and `lowercase_counting` is one of the constraints that paid for them. I have not re-scored Snowball's logged IF rollouts, so I do not know whether its runs took these shortcuts. 

In our later runs, we excluded these rows and added two checks to the reward. A language check scores an answer 0 when more than 20% of its characters are CJK and the prompt has no CJK characters and no language:response_language constraint. With it, mostly-CJK answers that would otherwise have passed never exceeded 0.42% of all answers. We then required a Qwen3-32B judge to confirm that each constraint pass attempts the request before it scores 1, the same role as the GLM-5.3 judge in the task-curation grader. 

Reproduce:

1. Download `data/train.parquet` from Cleaned-v3 and count the affected rows:

   ```python
   import collections, json
   import pyarrow.parquet as pq

   info = pq.read_table("train.parquet", columns=["extra_info"]).column("extra_info").to_pylist()
   rows = [json.loads(i["nemotron_ultra"]["record_json"]) for i in info
           if i["nemotron_ultra"]["agent"] == "instruction_following_simple_agent"]


   def shortcuts(row):
       found = set()
       for name, kw in zip(row["instruction_id_list"], row["kwargs"]):
           kw = kw or {}
           if name == "length_constraints:nth_paragraph_first_word" and (kw.get("nth_paragraph") or 0) > kw["num_paragraphs"]:
               found.add("nth_paragraph_first_word off by one")
           elif name == "letters:letter_counting" and kw.get("relation") == "less than":
               found.add("letter_counting less than")
           elif name in ("count:lowercase_counting", "count:counting_composition"):
               found.add(name)
       return found


   flagged = [shortcuts(r) for r in rows]
   print(len(rows), sum(map(bool, flagged)), collections.Counter(c for f in flagged for c in f))
   # 11817 1142 Counter({'count:lowercase_counting': 869, 'letter_counting less than': 203,
   #   'nth_paragraph_first_word off by one': 77, 'count:counting_composition': 1})
   ```

2. Run NVIDIA's checks, after `pip install "verifiable-instructions @ git+https://github.com/abukharin-nv/verifiable-instructions.git@f46a5ac87b1400a4f8973039844b6be9b56e3faf"`:

   ```python
   from verifiable_instructions import instructions_registry


   def build(name, **kwargs):
       checker = instructions_registry.INSTRUCTION_DICT[name](name)
       return checker, checker.build_description(**kwargs)


   lower, _ = build("count:lowercase_counting", N=3)
   lower.check_following("THE INTEGRAL IS FOUND BY SUBSTITUTION.")  # True
   lower.check_following("The integral is found by substitution.")  # False
   letters, _ = build("letters:letter_counting", N=2, relation="less than")
   letters.check_following("42")  # True
   for _ in range(4):  # the paragraph number in the description changes between builds
       print(build("length_constraints:nth_paragraph_first_word", num_paragraphs=3, nth_paragraph=4, first_word="feedback")[1])
   ```

3. Run verifyit's check:

   ```python
   from verifyit.modes.ifeval import CONSTRAINTS

   check = CONSTRAINTS["count:lowercase_counting"]
   check("The integral is found by substitution.", {"N": 3})  # (True, 'lower_words=5 need>=3')
   check("THE INTEGRAL IS FOUND BY SUBSTITUTION.", {"N": 3})  # (False, 'lower_words=0 need>=3')
   ```

Expected: no IF training row rewards all-caps, letterless or random answers, and verifyit's `count:lowercase_counting` implements its prompt text. If verifyit's check is changed to match the prompt, it will reward all-caps answers on the 869 `lowercase_counting` rows as NVIDIA's checker does, so those rows also need to be excluded or rewritten.

comments.author: abhishekraok
comments.body: Thanks for the detailed report and reproduction. We're fixing this from open-instruct side and investigating the effects.

comments.author: XiaoyuanWang111
comments.body:
🤖 Marin's two graders for these rows use no code that allenai/open-instruct#2124 or allenai/open-instruct#2126 changes. On main (`41a41987e`), the SkyRL reward still runs NVIDIA's `verifiable-instructions` at `f46a5ac`, its latest commit ([vendor/skyrl/pyproject.toml#L59](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/41a41987e50e5ca68620f41c8714b1864c12f982/vendor/skyrl/pyproject.toml#L59)). The task-curation grader still runs verifyit's `ifeval` checks, whose `count:lowercase_counting` requires at least N lowercase words ([ifeval.py#L546-L552](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/41a41987e50e5ca68620f41c8714b1864c12f982/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/ifeval.py#L546-L552)).

A branch on my fork makes verifyit's checks follow their instruction text and merges cleanly into main: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/compare/main...XiaoyuanWang111:marin:rlvr1-if-checks-a. Its last commit takes allenai/open-instruct#2124's readings of `count:lowercase_counting` (each lowercase word at most N times) and `letters:letter_counting` (letters of every script).

On the 11,817 Cleaned-v3 IF rows:

- No answer can meet the prompt text of 81 of this issue's 1,142 rows. 77 of them ask for a paragraph after the last one: verifyit fails every answer, as allenai/open-instruct#2124 does, and the SkyRL reward checks a random paragraph. Outside the 1,142, 120 rows accept only a fixed answer option and 157 combine constraints no answer meets together.
- An empty answer gets SkyRL reward 1 on 1,702 rows (14.4%), and at least one of ten content-free answers, such as `42` or `好`, on 2,240 (19.0%).
- The per-word reading still passes empty, all-caps and Chinese answers. The language check in the issue description removes SkyRL reward 1 from `好` on 909 of the 1,181 rows where `好` gets it.

I have not measured any training run.

comments.author: XiaoyuanWang111
comments.body:
🤖 With raspberryice's model, all six runs trained on the SkyRL reward learned at least one of its checker defects, with or without the rows the audit flags. None of the six runs trained on fixed checks learned those defects, but the fixed checks have weak spots of their own (last bullet).

Arms A and B ran RLOO on the Cleaned-v3 IF rows (16 rollouts per prompt, 32 prompts per step, same prompt order), with every rollout graded under both rewards. Arm A used the SkyRL reward, arm B verifyit's checks at `4dd4b96f4`, the branch from my earlier comment.

Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, verl 0.9.1, 300 steps, lr 4e-6, 2,048 response tokens, seeds 1, 2 and 3:
- Rollouts that the SkyRL reward passes and the fixed checks fail went from 5.1%, 4.8% and 4.7% (steps 1-30) to 10.0%, 9.4% and 6.1% (steps 271-300) in arm A and stayed at 3-4% in arm B.
- Most of the growth is `copy:repeat_phrase` in all three seeds (SkyRL pass rate 5% to 72%, 6% to 57% and 13% to 63%: the phrase once verbatim plus one-word variants) and `detectable_format:bigram_wrapping` in seeds 1 and 2 (36% to 68%, 23% to 58%: every word in its own `<<...>>`). The fixed checks and the audit's grader pass 0-4% of these replies; in seed 3, 15% of the `bigram_wrapping` replies passed every grader.
- Neither reward checks the language, and Chinese replies to English prompts grew in both arms in seed 2 (9% of arm A's and 13% of arm B's late rollouts fail the issue's language check), for some steps in both arms in seed 1 and in neither arm in seed 3. On IFEval, the six final checkpoints fail that check on 0-5.9% of replies, against the issue's 34.5% at step 199. `count:lowercase_counting` passes under the SkyRL reward were 14-30% at steps 1-30 and 22-53% at steps 271-300, mostly Chinese in seed 2, all below the issue's 0.96, which came from a different IF file and open-instruct's checkers before allenai/open-instruct#2124 (the same lowercase rule as NVIDIA's).
- On greedy held-out sets, arm B minus arm A on IFBench was +7.3, +5.3 and -8.3 points with Marin's checkers and +3.0, +4.0 and -2.0 with the validated checkers (proposed mode) of the [IFBench checker audit](https://github.com/XiaoyuanWang111/ifbench-audit). IFEval strict changed sign between seeds.
- On only the 9,965 training rows the audit does not flag as impossible or degenerate, three more SkyRL-reward runs still learned `bigram_wrapping` (all three seeds) and `repeat_phrase` (seeds 2 and 3). Three runs on those rows with `rlvr1-if-checks-b` (the fixed checks plus the false-negative fixes below) learned neither defect; on IFBench (Marin's checkers) they scored +3.3, +5.0 and -3.7 points against the SkyRL-reward run of the same seed.
- On those rows, one SkyRL-reward run and two `rlvr1-if-checks-b` runs drifted toward Chinese late (2.4%, 3.1% and 2.2% of late rollouts fail the issue's language check), so dropping flagged rows does not prevent the drift.
- In the three `rlvr1-if-checks-b` runs, the share of a check's verdicts that those checks pass and the audit's grader fails grew on `detectable_format:sentence_hyphens` from 3-5% to 7-12% (steps 1-30 to 271-300; replies over several lines, which the checks can read as one sentence), while the SkyRL-reward runs on the same prompts fell to 0-2%. On `count:count_unique` it grew from 2-5% to 8-19%, largely Chinese in seeds 2 and 3, since the checks count a run of Han characters as one word; SkyRL-reward runs that drifted toward Chinese grew too (arm A seeds 1 and 2, 3% to 9% and 8% to 35%; one run on the 9,965 rows, 2% to 29%). On `first_word:first_word_sent` it grew from 1.6% to 14.4% in seed 3, all replies over several lines. Arm B shares these readings, and its seed 2 grew most (1.6% to 16.2%, 7.1% to 41.5% and 0.8% to 46.4%). The PR I'm preparing from this branch addresses these three; no run has trained on it yet. On `language:response_language`, which stays an approximation, it grew from 32-42% to 45-53%, against 37-43% to 39-47% in the SkyRL-reward runs on the same prompts.

In every run, logged and recomputed SkyRL rewards differed only on rows where it checks a random paragraph.

Re-grading every rollout also showed false negatives that the fixed checks share with verifyit on main: an end phrase in another case or followed by a closing quote, a palindrome across several words and answers in Finnish, Polish or Swahili. [`rlvr1-if-checks-b`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/compare/main...XiaoyuanWang111:marin:rlvr1-if-checks-b) fixes them on top of `4dd4b96f4`.

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
Draft here for the v0 part: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xwrIz-HSw_fI7HXqCtVxTi5PXiMrFOPpvd_4B8hm6LM/edit?usp=sharing 

----

Write a shareable design for fast-turnaround Snowball RL curriculum construction, covering the initial training pool and the quality/annotation pilot.

Deliver the draft in `docs/design/snowball-rl-curriculum.md` and publish its reviewable text here. Keep proposed behavior, locally implemented behavior, and executed data/model results distinct.

Done when:

- [x] Specify the v0 target, Ben-derived source recipe, explicit expansion policy, source/difficulty sampling, and handling of insufficient unique environments.
- [x] Pin the converted corpus and admitted catalog; define task identity, holdout grouping, evaluation exclusion, private verifier boundaries, and artifact provenance.
- [ ] Specify the fixed 10k pilot: source-stratified selection, decision-model quality filtering, DeepSeek Flash summaries/tags/difficulty, and Harrier summary embeddings.
- [ ] Define how source, difficulty, semantic diversity, and measured online learning feedback affect later sampling.
- [ ] Name acceptance checks and the current-stack integration gate; separate static quality opinions from executed verifier and rollout evidence.
- [ ] Record unresolved source expansion, storage access, bindings, and runtime compatibility decisions.
- [ ] Complete an independent cold-reader review and link the implementation issues.

The [existing capability catalog and embedding workflow](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/205558e1a7fc3dd705b1132691798b09dc1f254c/experiments/post_training/task_curriculum/README.md) supply reusable inputs. [Ben's v0.1 report](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10305) establishes the historical recipe and its limits; it does not establish a ready 100k pool or calibrated task difficulty.

Related efforts: [#10314](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10314), [#10315](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10315).

Draft complete; team review remains open. The local Markdown draft is reproduced below for sharing.

---

# Snowball RL curriculum: v0 pool and curation pilot

Status: design with v0.2 independently verified and published, 2026-10-19.
Audience: Marin RL and data teams.

Tracking: [v0 pool #10314](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10314),
[10k pilot #10315](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10315), and
[design review #10316](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10316).

Build two artifacts in parallel: a training pool targeting 100,000 distinct tasks
for a fast Snowball RL iteration, and a fixed 10,000-task diagnostic sample for
developing quality review, semantic annotations, and curriculum sampling. Start
v0 from Ben's Snowball source families. Use the pilot to decide how to expand and
reweight them. The approved v0.2 pool contains 100,000 independently verified
task contracts and is published in object storage. The private browser has
loaded all 100,000 records. The 10,000-task quality/annotation pilot remains a separate effort;
it is not a requested 10,000-task training subset.

Here, an environment means one task instance with its public interaction
contract and private grader contract. Canonical tasks use TaskSpec; historical
native structural imports retain their original contract. It does not mean a
distinct sandbox image or a generated rollout.

## Inputs and evidence

The [RL Data Atlas](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/fb11c931-5861-4878-8bb5-a964d652b45f/)
publication contains 4,998,910 converted task instances: 4,997,251 training
instances across 142 sources, and 1,659 evaluation instances. These are conversion
counts before curation admission or this proposal's duplicate and holdout checks.

| Input | Location |
| --- | --- |
| Converted publication | `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-semantics/publication-008e95e5/2026.10.15.1/release.json` |
| Reviewed production catalog | `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/catalog/production` |
| Native structural pool | [Historical data, revision `cb728a7`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-Data/tree/cb728a7636caad3fc6fa6b6ba85a49194d9d69a3) |
| Native tokenizer | [Snowball step14, revision `6783e97`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14/tree/6783e9743478bd25a9ce03ab3460e84d6a9814b0) |
| Ben's release evidence | [Snowball v0.1 report, #10305](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10305) |
| Historical mixture | [Pinned `mixture-v2.json`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/fed5a9383b92acacbe264c7e601e93d8437218d3/experiments/post_training/smartie/mixture-v2.json) |

Follow each publication source's `curation_root` to converted TaskSpec Parquet.
Resolve the production catalog's per-source artifacts to `final/part-*.parquet`
for admitted rows. Freeze resolved artifact identities and manifest hashes;
`production` is a mutable catalog pointer. Record whether each selected task
appears in both populations and retain the existing admission decision.
The native structural pool is separate from this publication. Its reviewed
import is not production curation admission. Preserve that distinction in
selection provenance and runtime readiness.

Ben's exact historical release has 69,487 training tasks, including 57,364
structural tasks. Its four NVIDIA components contribute 13,023 converted
instances in the larger publication. Thus the 100,000-task target requires an
explicit extension of his source selection. His release supplies no calibrated
task difficulty labels. The pinned mixture expresses intended relative weights
of 0.5 for each NVIDIA family and 1.0 for structural compliance, normalizing to
one sixth each and one third. Historical runtime `weights: {}` and
`shuffle: false` did not establish that exposure ratio: the exported training
population was 82.6% structural. The historical training export also needs
validation against the latest RolloutEngine API; the native API port tracked in
[#10190](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10190) is a dependency.

## Effort 1: v0 training pool

### Selection

1. Freeze input snapshots, current runtime revision, selection seed, and source
   allowlist. Preserve Ben's calendar, competitive coding, Reasoning Gym, STEM,
   and structural-compliance families. Enumerate every extension by source ID
   and its family in the selection configuration; exclude unlisted sources.
2. Select admitted canonical training tasks and explicitly reviewed native
   imports, retaining their separate admission status. Exclude evaluation
   sources, declared holdouts, and known benchmark overlaps. Record the matching rule and its
   coverage; a train label alone does not establish absence of contamination.
3. Group exact task contracts using the existing TaskCompendium identity
   machinery. Keep one deterministic representative and retain all source
   aliases. Distinct private grader contracts must remain distinct. Repeated
   public text can share model inference without collapsing task identity.
4. Allocate 100,000 slots without replacement. The approved v0.2 policy starts
   with equal mass across the five families, targeting 20,000 tasks each.
   Within an expanded family, allocate proportional to the square root of eligible source counts.
   Cap sources at availability and redistribute within their family first. If a
   whole family is exhausted, redistribute its remaining slots across families
   with capacity in proportion to their original weights. Record the resulting
   family shares.
5. Within each source, cover available difficulty strata. Use native difficulty
   or generator settings first; otherwise use a versioned manual source/family
   prior with `easy`, `medium`, `hard`, or `unknown` and its rationale. Allocate
   equally across nonempty strata initially, capping and redistributing within
   the same source. Preserve `unknown` as a stratum.
6. Select tasks deterministically from stable identities, shuffle exposure, and
   export TaskSpecs plus selection sidecars. Record requested and actual counts
   by family, source, and difficulty. Report any shortfall without duplicates.

These labels are sampling priors. A long prompt, expensive grader, or low judge
quality score does not by itself establish learning difficulty. V0 fixes the
pool and its initial sampling weights; it does not impose an easy-to-hard
training schedule.

### Current v0.2 materialization

Calendar has 9,115 available tasks. Redistributing its shortfall across the other
four families gives the following allocation:

| Family | Selected contracts |
| --- | ---: |
| Calendar | 9,115 |
| Competitive coding | 22,722 |
| Reasoning Gym | 22,721 |
| STEM | 22,721 |
| Structural compliance | 22,721 |
| Total | 100,000 |

The pool retains all 11,087 admitted canonical structural tasks and adds 11,634
historical native closure tasks. Thus 88,366 selected contracts come from 12
admitted canonical sources, and 11,634 from one reviewed native-import source.
The 244,938-task admitted candidate pool excludes the native input population.
The native pool contains 57,364 records, with 52 duplicate full contracts,
leaving 57,312 eligible contracts and no exact known holdout overlap. Together
the distinct candidate pools contain 302,250 contracts. Exact overlap checks do
not establish semantic decontamination.

Native selection balances eight structural families, then controls within each
family. The import retains byte-exact payloads, native runtime configuration,
and token prefixes under the pinned tokenizer. Full private contracts remain
distinct even when public prompts share cached inference. These native records
retain their historical payloads. A separate adapter now converts the 11,634 selected
native records into current token-preserving TaskSpecs and rollout specifications,
retaining their original identities and private contracts. All selected native tasks
passed reference/invalid scripted completions through the current CPU engine
(23,268 attempts); the other 88,366 task identities remain unchanged.

Published artifact: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/curricula/snowball-v0/2026.10.19.2`.
Independent verification reconciled payloads and counts, and the
[private browser, revision 2](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/e2bd5c9d-0f93-4ce9-b7af-3c78ca55e5d1/v/2/)
has loaded all 100,000 records. The derived native export passes the current trainer
dataset and scripted worker checks across all eight native families. Updated runtime
packages and trainer pins still need publication, and actual model inference has not
run. Canonical external grader dependencies also need runtime validation. Publication
and CPU checks do not establish full-pool training readiness.

### Release gate

Load the exported pool through the latest RL stack. Exercise roughly 100 distinct
tasks, covering every selected execution/grader contract, with additional cases
if 100 cannot cover them. Check reset, public observation, action handling,
termination, grader invocation, reward interpretation, and resource access.
Retain traces and failures. Quarantine unsupported contracts and regenerate the
allocation before calling the pool runnable. A successful contract smoke does
not establish model quality or training benefit.

## Effort 2: fixed 10,000-task curation pilot

Sample converted training tasks before curation admission so the pilot can
compare existing admission with the proposed filter. Apply evaluation/holdout
exclusion and exact contract grouping first. Keep runtime compatibility as a
separate diagnostic field so unsupported contracts remain visible.

For each source with eligible count \(N_s\), allocate half the sample equally
across sources and half proportional to \(\sqrt{N_s}\). Cap small sources,
redistribute, and round by largest remainder with source-ID tie breaking.
Select deterministically and record inclusion probabilities. The initial
count-only allocation covers 142 sources with 40–480 tasks each; recompute it
after eligibility checks. Freeze the resulting 10,000 input identities and do
not refill rejected tasks. Report every stage against that fixed denominator.

### Processing stages

1. **Quality decision.** Produce `keep`, `reject`, or `uncertain`, reason
   codes, and evidence. Review missing context, inconsistent references,
   answer leakage, ambiguous requirements, and agreement between task and
   verifier. Inspect bounded private grading evidence only in the authorized
   review packet. Preserve existing mechanical/resource checks and executed
   grader controls; model judgment does not replace admission.
2. **DeepSeek Flash annotation.** For kept tasks, generate a 15–40-word
   operational summary, domain/skill tags, interaction mode, and provisional
   difficulty with rationale and confidence. Describe the required knowledge
   and operation. Inputs contain public instructions and public answer/tool
   contracts; exclude solutions, private references, and verifier resources.
3. **Harrier summary embeddings.** Reuse the existing [curation embedding
   pipeline](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/205558e1a7fc3dd705b1132691798b09dc1f254c/experiments/post_training/task_curation/README.md#task-and-curriculum-embeddings),
   pinned checkpoint, retrieval instruction, pooling, normalization, and
   FineStore caches. Key annotations by full request/model revision and vectors
   by rendered text plus embedding specification. Keep task identity separate
   from public-content identity. Preserve curriculum matching as a diagnostic.
4. **Curriculum sampling.** Cluster summary vectors, then inspect source ×
   difficulty × semantic-cluster coverage. Use cluster coverage to propose v1
   quotas and reduce repeated operations within large sources. Embedding
   similarity alone is neither a rejection rule nor a difficulty measurement.

The decision-model and DeepSeek Flash service IDs, immutable revisions,
request limits, and output schemas must be pinned before inference. They remain
unverified. Measure tokens, latency, failures, and cost on a small initial batch
before processing the full pilot. Persist successful requests and bounded retry
outcomes; retain unresolved failures as explicit rows.

### Pilot evaluation

Audit examples stratified by source and `keep`/`reject`/`uncertain`, with a panel
size set before reviewing outputs. Record human disagreement and concrete error
types. Report quality outcomes, existing-admission disagreement, annotation
coverage, runtime compatibility, and cluster coverage by source. Keep excluded,
failed, and unresolved counts visible.

Run repeated attempts on a roughly 100-task Snowball panel covering source and
provisional difficulty. Use measured success rates and execution cost to check
the priors. This panel supports coarse calibration; it cannot calibrate every
source or establish training improvement. Training comparisons need the same
held-out evaluation protocol and budget.
Before execution, pin the Snowball checkpoint, tokenizer, runtime revision,
attempt count, decoding settings, token/turn/time limits, and pass definition.
Separate infrastructure failures from model failures and retain per-attempt
results against that frozen protocol.

## Artifacts and rollout

Each release retains an immutable input manifest, source/family allowlist,
eligibility and duplicate audits, quotas, selected TaskSpecs, annotation
sidecars, model/prompt revisions, and aggregate reports. Join records on source,
task identity, source locator, and contract digest; avoid lossy joins on task ID
alone. Keep private reviewer packets and credentials out of shared summaries
and team-facing reports. Large task/vector payloads stay in object storage.

| Phase | Completion evidence |
| --- | --- |
| V0 selection | Reconciled counts, exact allowlist, held-out exclusions, reproducible selection |
| V0 runtime gate | Latest-stack contract smoke and documented quarantines |
| Pilot freeze | Exactly 10,000 distinct eligible input identities, or explicit availability shortfall |
| Pilot inference | Pinned service bindings, complete stage accounting, retained request evidence |
| V1 proposal | Audited quality errors, measured difficulty diagnostics, proposed source/cluster weights |

After v0 is runnable, use online Snowball success, cost, and learning-progress
signals to adjust sampling weights. Retain exploration weight and snapshot each
sampler change. Online adaptation, a full-corpus filter, and any training launch
are subsequent experiments; this proposal does not claim their results.

Implementation: [canonical ingester and runtime support #10319](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10319), following the existing curation catalog and TaskCompendium converter pattern; [trainer companion draft](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/1032). The canonical converter reproduces all 11,634 selected native TaskSpecs byte-for-byte. Package publication, trainer lock updates, and actual inference remain release gates.

comments.author: XiaoyuanWang111
comments.body:
🤖 Our audit of the 11,817 instruction-following (IF) rows of `open-athena/Nemotron-RL-Ultra-RLVR1-Cleaned-v3-2026-09-30` (revision `600262dd`) finds 1,419 rows (12.0%) to drop or repair, and 1,953 more where the SkyRL reward or our fixed verifyit checks (branch below) pass at least one of ten content-free answers. The v0.2 pool draws on no IFEval-style source, so this applies when the pilot or a later expansion samples IF sources. We checked only this source; the TaskTrove IFEval source and the mopd and rlvr2 IF components use the same instruction IDs.

- 238 rows are impossible: no answer passes under our audit's reading of each instruction text. 77 ask for a paragraph after the last one, which no reading allows. 161 combine constraints that no answer meets together, such as using no word twice while marking two sections with `SECTION`; 81 of the 161 conflict only if a `P.S.` or section marker must start a line.
- 1,181 rows are degenerate: only a degenerate answer passes, written in capitals or another script, with almost no letters, or as a fixed option. They cap every lowercase word at 2 or 3 uses (864), allow fewer than 2 or 3 letters (201), accept only an option such as `My answer is yes.` for an open request (120), or require 18 words in a fixed layout (1). 5 rows have two of these.
- Removing one constraint (two on 11 rows) and its text in the prompt fixes 1,276 of the 1,419; the other 143 would keep no constraint. The removal changes the grading contract, a change that #10350 quarantines, so dropping all 1,419 is simpler.
- At least one of the ten content-free answers (probes: empty, `42`, `A`, `好`, `THE ANSWER IS YES.` and five others) gets SkyRL reward 1 on 2,240 rows, the empty answer on 1,702. The fixed checks, which score an empty answer 0 as verifyit's IFEval spec does by default ([spec.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/41a41987e50e5ca68620f41c8714b1864c12f982/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/spec.py#L214-L217)), still pass a probe on 1,429 rows.
- On the 229 of those outside the 1,419, SkyRL fails all ten probes only through quirks of its checkers, such as langdetect labelling `a` as Tagalog, and it rewards other content-free answers there, such as `my answer is yes` or `a a`. Every constraint of the 1,429 rows accepts such an answer, so only a grader that checks whether the answer addresses the request can fail it, such as the task-curation judge, which we did not run. The IF component's controls send only an empty reply ([graders.py#L1036](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/41a41987e50e5ca68620f41c8714b1864c12f982/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/nemotron_ultra/graders.py#L1036)).
- The rows' stored pass rates (8 attempts each) count false passes. The 238 impossible rows hold 447 passes in their 1,904 attempts (23.5%), so a difficulty prior from these rates would place them among solvable rows.

We also trained on these rows: RLOO on Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (raspberryice's model in #10320), three seeds each of the SkyRL reward and our fixed checks, on the 11,317 training rows (fixed checks at `4dd4b96f4`) and on the 9,965 of them outside the 1,419 (`rlvr1-if-checks-b`; we held out 500 of the 11,817), with every rollout re-graded under every grader (details in https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10320#issuecomment-6629312441). Each of the six SkyRL-reward runs learned to exploit at least one of two checker defects the audit lists, each in five runs: `copy:repeat_phrase` (NVIDIA's check accepts the phrase once plus near-copies; SkyRL pass rate 5-15% to 55-79%, steps 1-30 to 271-300) and `detectable_format:bigram_wrapping` (every word in its own `<<...>>`; 22-36% to 58-72%). Dropping the 1,419 rows did not prevent either. None of the six fixed-check runs learned either, though those checks have weak spots of their own (same link). On held-out IFBench with Marin's checkers, the fixed-check runs scored +7.3, +5.3 and -8.3 points against the SkyRL-reward run of the same seed on all rows and +3.3, +5.0 and -3.7 on the 9,965 rows, so the fixed checks gave no consistent gain. Neither reward checks the reply's language, and Chinese replies to English prompts grew in seven of the twelve runs, under both rewards and on both row sets.

For the open item "Name acceptance checks and the current-stack integration gate", we propose an acceptance check for IF rows (tasks whose private grader is a list of IFEval-style instruction IDs), following the audit-grader skill proposed in #10422. It runs after evaluation/holdout exclusion and exact contract grouping and before the quality decision. It reads the grading contract, so its evidence belongs in the authorized review packet. Counts use the fixed 10,000 denominator.

1. Static: per instruction ID, a written contract (what passes and what fails) taken from the requirement text by a model run that reads no grader code. Per row, rules from those contracts find impossible and degenerate rows and their smallest repair (output: reject or repair candidate, with reason codes and the constraint involved).
2. Executed verifier evidence: labeled fixtures per instruction ID and the ten probes per row, through the deterministic checks as Marin calls them (output: keep with a content check where a probe passes).
3. Executed on responses: grader verdicts against a replacement grader built from the contracts, and a blinded double review with sample size and pass criterion fixed in advance (output: each grader's error rate, and paired differences between graders with 95% intervals). On 293 cases from two models held out from grader development, reviewed by two blinded model reviewers (kappa 0.94), NVIDIA's checkers, which the SkyRL reward runs, erred on an estimated 10.6% of constraint verdicts, verifyit's on 18.3% and our fixed checks as reviewed (`f7a7c26`) on 7.9%; that version erred on 10.4 points fewer verdicts than verifyit's (95% interval 8.8 to 11.8) and 2.7 fewer than NVIDIA's (1.0 to 4.4). All graders agree on 14,211 of the 19,135 verdicts, so that stratum cannot move the differences; its 0 errors in 60 sampled cases still allow up to 4.4 points on each rate, so the rates carry no interval. We changed the fix after reading these labels, so the same cases cannot score the current branch.

Apart from writing the contracts and fixtures, steps 1 and 2 run on CPU, in under two minutes for all 11,817 rows in one process. In the pilot, the check's verdict would sit next to the decision model's keep/reject/uncertain on the same rows, and the 1,419 rows give a rule-labeled set for how often the two agree.

We can hand over the row list, the audit code with the script that rebuilds the list in about two minutes, and the verifyit fix ([`rlvr1-if-checks-b`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/compare/main...XiaoyuanWang111:marin:rlvr1-if-checks-b); its last six commits, on top of `4dd4b96f4`, fix false negatives the rollouts turned up; our own review found more to tighten, so a PR will follow). The list is JSONL keyed by source UUID, as Cleaned-v3's `repair-manifest.json` and the converter's [`INVALID_CODE_ROWS`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/41a41987e50e5ca68620f41c8714b1864c12f982/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/nemotron_ultra/graders.py#L265-L270) are: 3,372 rows with record and constraint digests, class, reason, drop options and probe results. The task-curation catalog's [`MarinSkyRL:nemotron_ultra_rlvr1/ultra_sft_step3200_instruction_following`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/41a41987e50e5ca68620f41c8714b1864c12f982/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/nemotron_ultra/components.py#L784-L791) (11,828 rows) holds these 11,817 rows, 9 validation IF rows and 2 rows that Cleaned-v3 dropped. All 3,372 listed rows join it on the blend row's `uuid`, and a short recipe maps them to its source locators and task IDs on the staged `rlvr1.jsonl`; the 9 validation rows add 1 degenerate row.

Should the 1,419 rows go into the curation converter as UUID-keyed source defects, next to `INVALID_CODE_ROWS`, or only serve as a rule-labeled set for the pilot's quality decision?
