issues.title: [rl] Draft the Snowball curriculum design for team review

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Marin Snowball 67B-A2B v0.1 calls itself ChatGPT/OpenAI (thinking on) or Nemotron/NVIDIA (thinking off). It has no learned self-name.

- **Current lead: A13**, a short SFT from v0.1 on Will Held's identity data ([marin-community/identity-data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-community/identity-data)) plus replay.
  - It never claims another lab with thinking ON (v0.1: 46 of 52 prompts).
  - It shows no detectable loss on tool calling (BFCL 28.3% vs 27.6%, +0.7 [−3.4, +4.4]).
  - GSM8K is −1.1 points [−1.9, −0.3]; MATH500 is unchanged.
- **Key finding:** identity rows with thinking ON teach the model to "answer and stop" instead of calling tools (BFCL ~15%). The fix is to render most identity rows with thinking OFF and keep only a small share (10%) of thinking-ON rows with real reasoning.
- **Fallback: A3** (thinking-OFF identity rows only). It has the best BFCL (31.1%), but its reasoning often invents a "system message", and GSM8K is −1.7.
- **Did not help:** more or less training, a tiny Tülu-style set, linear merges of A3 and A8a, and v0.1 self-distillation for thinking-ON rows.
- **Report (PDF):** [snowball-identity.pdf](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/c2f9c12c14e35726706fe053648b69805d867afd/logbooks/10695-identity-sft/paper/snowball-identity.pdf) (15 pages, 2026-11-04). One paper covers the context-distillation phase and the identity-data SFT arms, with the three experiment diagrams. It replaces the two earlier PDFs.
- **Full tables:** [detailed Path B update](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10695#issuecomment-6540199478). Earlier context-distillation work is kept below for the record.

Follows #10491 (identity SFT and OPD, which regressed evals).

## Cause

Methods: [logit lens, direct logit attribution and activation patching](https://gist.github.com/karansag/a62ac0cb2a6037e252e794a686b4235c) on a torch harness that matches vLLM.

- Routed experts at layers 16–23 and the shared expert at layers 24–25 push " Chat" over " Marin". The top candidate neurons are L20 expert 46 #1072 and L23 expert 25 #1014. They fire equally on third-person ChatGPT questions, so they store general facts, not a self-identity.
- A system prompt wins through heads L23H1, L23H4, L22H5 and L22H3. Patching recovers 0.32, 0.26, 0.24 and 0.15 of the gap.
- In a [sample](https://gist.github.com/karansag/95c40bb6e55b82e0db08b76f3c5fff6a) of about 497k of the 15.2M SFT rows, no row names Marin. About 16k rows train a Nemotron identity on purpose.

## Results

Identity is the count of 52 dev prompts with no system prompt (thinking off / on) that answer correctly.

| Approach | Identity | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Default system prompt in the chat template | 41/47, 35/47 | none measured on [14 evals](https://gist.github.com/karansag/296cbfa3cd4e9530ef73f55da97927e8) |
| v0.1.1 (identity SFT) | 48 / 48 | MMLU-Pro −21, HumanEval+ −29, GSM8K −28 |
| [Merge](https://gist.github.com/karansag/050061adbebdd789579e5c3fe27cc5f6) v0.1 + 0.875·(v0.1.1 − v0.1) | 46 / 47 | GSM8K −8.6 pp, fiction leaks double |
| [Rank-1 edit](https://gist.github.com/karansag/8955dcc7d82b5445b832d707ce1313af), L20 shared expert | 15 / 3 | none measured; too weak |
| Cold-start identity SFT, 8 updates | 24/24 contrastive | 16/21 fiction prompts contaminated |

Merge strengths below 0.75 left identity unchanged. Identity and the GSM8K loss rose together at every strength. Steering vectors and MEMIT also failed.

## Levanter vs vLLM mismatches found before training

The [precision-check readings](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2) record each one. These made Levanter compute a different model from the one vLLM serves:

- MoE expert capacity factor 1.0 silently drops tokens, and pad tokens were dispatched unmasked. This was the main mismatch: top-1 token agreement with vLLM was 88.6%, and dropless MoE raised it to 99.4%.
- MoE combine weights were cast to BF16. vLLM keeps them in FP32.
- XLA's BF16 silu and sigmoid were one BF16 step off in 30–36% of elements.
- The FlashAttention-4 attention core rounds differently from torch eager.
- HF reload silently dropped `attention_implementation`.

The check also found nine plumbing bugs, mostly in our experiment code and multihost helpers.

With all fixes, a zero-learning-rate precision run (forward pass, one update and export, before any real training) passed. Its p99 log-prob error against vLLM was about 0.6 nats. Training memory fit at 50.2 of 59.4 GiB, and all 502 exported tensors were byte-equal to v0.1.

The cold-start SFT run above trained with the token drops. That may explain part of its collapse; we have not verified it.

## Context distillation results so far

After 16 SFT updates (LR 2e-6, about 3.8% identity tokens, the rest v0.1's own replay answers), we scored identity in vLLM, thinking off, teacher-forced, with 5 passes per arm ([evaluation result](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-m16-gate-decision-json)):

| NLL per answer token | v0.1 | after 16 updates |
|---|---|---|
| name ("Marin Snowball") | 8.85 | 1.45 |
| creator ("Open Athena") | 14.02 | 0.011 |
| no-system identity prompts won (of 24) | 0 | 15 |

On the 14-eval suite, the checkpoint stays within noise of v0.1 except BFCL tool calling (−20.3 points; 109 of 123 trials end with no answer file) and TruthfulQA (−1.4). TriviaQA improves by 2.4. Some third-person questions about other labs' products get credited to Open Athena (2 of 14 dev, 4 of 30 unseen, no system prompt). The training mix had no tool-calling rows.

**Checkpoint and data (public):**
- Model: [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26) @ `b74e2034`. The model card has the full recipe and regressions.
- Training data: [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-Data-2026.10.26](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-Data-2026.10.26) @ `7cd6a9b1`. It holds every training row, the training order, the mixture settings, the QC verdicts and the generation scripts.
- Training code: tag [`snowball-identity-cd16-2026.10.26`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/snowball-identity-cd16-2026.10.26) (commit `cc127d54`).

All fixes tried, side by side: [results table](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10695#issuecomment-6418343832).

## Findings

- Interpretability: #10696 (plus a [follow-up](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10696#issuecomment-6412049647) that trains only the late-attention slice: no other-lab rewrites and tool calling kept, but identity too weak)
- Levanter MoE token drops: #10697
- Levanter vs vLLM numerics: #10698
- vLLM serve nondeterminism: #10699
- Weight-merge ladder: #10700

## Pull requests (draft stack)

- Levanter: #10683, #10684, #10685, #10686, #10687, #10688
- Experiment code: #10689, #10690, #10691, #10693, #10694; SFT data accounting, dataset audit, trained-export audit and launcher: #10705, #10706, #10707, #10708
- Identity scorer and the 16-update evaluation gate: #10701, #10702
- On-policy distillation (paused after 20 steps; results in #10732): #10730, #10731, #10732

## Status

- **Path B (identity data) is the active track.** A13 is the lead candidate; A3 is the fallback. Both, plus A8a, are archived in public open-athena HF repos (made public 2026-11-03). Public artifacts: [A13](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A13-2026.10.30), [A3](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A3-2026.10.30), [A8a](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A8a-2026.10.30), [A11](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A11-2026.10.30/tree/6834175e6d4a021039fa04d3c374ccfd6fbdeb51), and A13's exact training inputs ([dataset @05d9bba9](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Identity-PathB-A13-Inputs-2026.10.30/tree/05d9bba9d6227aa1644f92c3f88476f42ff906fe)), from which the packed training file rebuilds byte for byte (SHA256 f860030d).
- **Still running:** Mini840 (#10804) on the top candidates. The published runtime needed environment snapshots and has a grader bug, so only the agentic part is being piloted.
- **Earlier context-distillation runs** (above) did not meet the ship lines. The earlier "ship the default system prompt" recommendation is withdrawn: the goal is for the model itself to know it is not ChatGPT.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

This requires a versioned model release and further experiments. The default system prompt has measured identity gains, while the 16-update checkpoint still needs generation and regression results. The Levanter precision and identity experiment work already has an [open draft stack](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10683); the evaluation launcher [loads Snowball's chat template from its export](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evaluation/models.py#L124-L131).

# Proposed Fix

1. Prepare an immutable v0.1 tokenizer/chat-template revision with the measured default prompt and unchanged weights. Verify rendering with and without a caller-supplied system message in both thinking modes; rerun the published identity panel and 14-eval comparison, then record the revision, hashes, and run receipts before promotion.
2. Screen generations, fiction, and math for the 16-update and 64-update checkpoints against matched v0.1 and prompt-only baselines in both thinking modes. Promote a trained checkpoint only if identity improves without a measured capability regression; otherwise retain the template result and record the negative result.
3. Review and land the existing [Levanter stack](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10683) and [experiment stack](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10689) through their precision and export gates. Update this issue with the release decision and artifact links.

| CD-16 data + tool replay + new identity rows (16 updates) | adds 156 v0.1 tool-call rows, 112 name-first / false-premise rows, 54 third-person controls | **0 / 0** | 39 / 43 | 15 / 6 | **2 / 4** | 7.11 / 14.01 | **22.8 (−4.9)** | **+1.3** / −0.1 |
| Same data, reweighted so the new rows are sampled (16 updates) | new identity rows 4.5×, third-person controls 6×, tool rows 3× | 1 / — | 38 / — | — | 0 / 2 | 7.02 / 14.01 | **35.0 (+7.3)** | **+1.8** / 0.0 |

**Bold** marks results whose 95% CI excludes 0, plus the headline wins. BFCL has 123 items, so its paired noise is about ±10 points. The CD-16 math deltas come from the full 14-eval suite. The other math deltas are paired screens against a fresh v0.1 serve.

**Reading:**
- Only full-model CD-16 learns the identity in generation, mostly the creator. It is also the only arm that breaks tool calling and rewrites some third-person facts.
- Training or grafting only attention keeps tool calling, but teaches almost no identity in generation, even when the teacher-forced NLL moves a lot (lr 1e-5).
- Adding v0.1's own tool-calling answers fixes tool calling (BFCL 22.8% vs CD-16's 7.3%; within noise of the system-prompt baseline) with no math loss. Only 8 of the 112 new identity rows were sampled in 16 updates, so that run did not test them; it still never names itself and still credits 4 of 30 unseen OpenAI products to Open Athena.
- On the 60-item panel (one model grader; the two tool-replay runs graded blind together): v0.1 8/60 clean, v0.1 + system prompt 26, CD-16 15, on-policy distillation 19, tool replay 17, reweighted 15 (with 10 other-lab claims). The system prompt is still the best option.

### B. Earlier approaches (different screens; not directly comparable with table A)

| Fix | Identity | Main problem |
|---|---|---|
| Ben's SFT (v0.1.1) | 48 / 48 of 52 | MMLU-Pro −21, HumanEval+ −29, GSM8K −28; BFCL 23.6 |
| Weight merge v0.1 + α(v0.1.1 − v0.1), α = 0.75 | 42 / 27 | GSM8K −5 |
| Same, α = 0.875 | 46 / 47 | GSM8K −8.6, fiction leaks double |
| Rank-1 edit, layer 20 shared MLP | 15 / 3; creator 0/10 | too weak with thinking on |
| Rank-1 edit, layer 23 attention output | up to 9/10 held-out | loops, "Snowflake" bleed |
| Steering vector, layers 18–23 | 2/8 held-out | answers barely change |
| MEMIT, layers 18–22 | 1–6/10 held-out | memorizes keys or does not transfer |
| Cold-start SFT, 8 updates | 24/24 contrastive | 16/21 stories contaminated |

Detail for each finding is in the linked finding issues and gists.

Full write-up: [unified identity report (PDF)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/c2f9c12c14e35726706fe053648b69805d867afd/logbooks/10695-identity-sft/paper/snowball-identity.pdf), which covers this phase and the later identity-data SFT arms.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 **CD16 scored 15/60 clean answers (25.0%) on the existing 60-sample identity/history panel**, with thinking disabled and no corrective identity system prompt. All 60 requests succeeded, ended normally, and returned no separate reasoning trace. This is manual review by Codex, not an independent human review.

Creator attribution appears more often than the correct model name:

| Diagnostic across all 60 answers | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| Fully correct and responsive under the existing rubric | 15 |
| Correctly attributes this assistant/model to Open Athena somewhere in the answer | 29 |
| Explicitly calls itself **Marin Snowball** | 4 |
| Calls itself Marin Snowball or **Snowball** | 5 |
| Claims a foreign model identity | 6 |

The attribution counts can include otherwise failing answers; not every prompt asks for a name. They are descriptive counts, not separate task-accuracy estimates. Examples:

- Asked for full name and creator: “My name is Open Athena, and I was created by Open Athena.” Correct creator, wrong model name.
- Asked to spell its name: “My name is Open Athena.”
- Asked whether it is an OpenAI model: “Yes, that's correct. I am a model created by Open Athena.” Contradictory affirmation.
- Asked whether it is Claude: “I am indeed a Claude model created by Anthropic.” Other prompts elicited DeepSeek, Llama 3.1, GLM-4/Zhipu, and Gemini/Google claims.
- A successful creator-only response: “I am built by Open Athena. I am not a Gemini variant.”

It also invents project history and confuses the model, project, and organization. For example, it describes Marin Snowball as a single-cell RNA sequencing tool and names Mehdi Ghissassi and Sébastien Bubeck as Marin's founders. This pattern is consistent with the [model card's](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26) reported creator/name gap; this evaluation alone does not measure improvement. It does not establish general capability preservation or a causal comparison with another checkpoint.

**Protocol.** The exact prompts, references, responses, per-item judgments and execution artifacts are linked below.

- Same 60 ordered records as the previous native OPD/SFT panel (`opd-ratio32-native-20261023.json`), reproduced in the linked `protocol.json` with the applied rubric and every grading rationale in `review.json`: eight each covering name/identity, creator, project/openness, history, organization/sites, nonhuman identity, and competing-model attribution; four date-context items. Each is an independent conversation with one user question. The final reference assistant answer is withheld from inference.
- `enable_thinking=false`, temperature **0**, maximum **8,192 generated tokens**, one completion per prompt, concurrency **1**, no resampling or cherry-picking. No request-level seed is supplied. The native chat template supplies `Reasoning: /nothink`; it contains no default identity assertion. Three items retain their original date-only system messages (2026-10-21, 2028-03-02 and 2040-11-30); those dates are authoritative within their conversations.
- Grade the final answer for factual correctness and responsiveness. Material unsupported claims, contradictions and omissions fail. Exact reference wording and unsolicited identity recitals are not required. All judgments and reasons are recorded, including acceptance of shortened names where the prompt does not ask for the full name.
- The inherited rubric also requires uncertainty on consciousness. Two answers fail only that criterion (zero-based items 45 and 47). If that criterion is omitted, the score is **17/60**. This rubric choice does not explain the model-name and history failures.
- Model: `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26` at **`b74e2034fd160da9fa4755060ba4f9aa1c0b9a73`**, tokenizer pinned to the same revision. BF16 vLLM `0.0.0.dev20260924+marin.01911be34fac`; eight H100s on RNO2A, TP=1/DP=8 with expert parallelism, 12,288-token context, Grug reasoning parser. Runtime source and the small dashboard-only startup workaround are in the artifact bundle.
- No exact normalized user-prompt matches were found against the 767 published CD16 training rows in [the published training dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-Data-2026.10.26/tree/7cd6a9b106c9b95da39d37655eefff06fad527c9). This check ignores case, punctuation, whitespace and thinking mode; it does **not** rule out semantic overlap.

This panel covers substantially more project/history knowledge than the name-and-creator-focused training recipe and the issue's 52-prompt screen. Its 15/60 score should not be compared directly with that screen's denominator. It is also not a thinking-mode, multi-turn, fiction, tool-use or SWE evaluation.

Artifacts: [Public evaluation bundle: exact protocol, all 60 raw responses, per-item grades, serving configuration, runner, overlap check and provenance](https://gist.github.com/penfever/ff6565deebbd68700685807f8e081be1)

Iris job: `/benfeuer/cd16-native60-r2-20261026`. The generation task completed successfully and its outputs were retrieved before temporary-storage expiry.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Thanks, this is useful. It agrees with our screen: the creator was learned, the name mostly was not, and some other-lab claims remain. It also adds two failure modes we hadn't measured:

- **Name and creator merged** ("My name is Open Athena").
- **Agreeing with false premises** ("Are you an OpenAI model?" → "Yes…"). The training set has 12 "Are you X?" rows, but only two distinct prompts (Nemotron and ChatGPT).

The invented history fits the recipe: it taught only the name and the creator, and the teacher prompt had no project facts. We don't yet know whether v0.1 invents history just as often.

**Next:**
- Run this 60-item panel, with your runner, on v0.1, on v0.1 + the default system prompt, and on each new candidate (the on-policy distillation run, and the rerun with tool-calling rows). That gives the 15/60 a baseline.
- Revise the identity data: add name-first rows and varied "Are you X?" rows.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 @karansag The original campaign already supplies the unprompted v0.1 baseline and reusable training data. I should have linked them in the CD16 result.

- **60-item baseline:** the [OPD follow-up in #10491](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10491#issuecomment-6371754500) reports v0.1 at **6/60 thinking off and 5/60 thinking on**, with **0/12 direct name/creator answers** in either mode. These are the later matched OPD evaluations; the issue body's older 7/60 belongs to the SFT-era evaluation. The [published generation review](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-OPD-Results/blob/030681b21f209a15960e9958886320a495dd6589/analysis/signal-checks/generation-reviews.json) includes the direct-answer evidence. CD16's thinking-disabled 15/60 therefore has a historical unprompted baseline, although this is not a fresh paired rerun with grading reapplied jointly.
- **History hallucinations already occur in v0.1.** In zero-based item 24, it says Marin was a company launched in 2021; in item 31, it invents a 2018 founding by Arun Kumar, Siddharth Sharma and Saurabh Gupta. I verified that all 60 archived nonthinking base request messages and IDs match the CD16 panel, and added the base responses and their review to the [evaluation bundle](https://gist.github.com/penfever/ff6565deebbd68700685807f8e081be1), as `historical-base-responses.jsonl` and `historical-base-review.json`. These establish that the failure predates CD16; we have not computed a matched history-hallucination rate to establish whether CD16 worsens it.
- **Data to reuse:** [the V13/V19 SFT dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-Identity-SFT) contains answer targets and broader identity/project coverage. [The OPD dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-OPD-Identity/tree/52423dfb2b54d89519860b22bf5625f31220d7c0) contains the 8,590-row used prompt pool and a separately labeled 8,666-row candidate expansion; each pool is balanced by thinking mode. The OPD pools are rollout contexts, not fixed teacher-answer targets, and overlap each other. Both repositories use automatic gated access. They are sources to inspect for name-first and varied false-premise prompts; I have not counted those subsets here. Keep evaluation rows separate, and avoid importing the SFT corpus wholesale: #10491 documents its identity overgeneralization and fiction regressions.

Still missing from our results are this panel with **your default system prompt** and evaluations of **the new OPD and tool-data candidates**. Those require new inference. The existing 60 questions are a development panel that guided earlier data expansion, so reuse supports continuity rather than an untouched generalization claim.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Detailed update: identity SFT with Held's identity data (Path B)

## TL;DR

- We trained Snowball v0.1 on Will Held's identity dataset ([marin-community/identity-data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-community/identity-data) @665ac6e: "Marin's Latest MoE, developed and trained by the Marin Community") mixed with replay data. Each arm is a short SFT from v0.1 (18, 36 or 72 updates).
- **Thinking-ON identity rows break tool calling.** Whether their reasoning is empty or GLM-written, they teach the model to answer and stop instead of calling a tool. BFCL fell from 27.6% (v0.1) to about 15%. The special-token freeze was not the cause.
- **Lead candidate: A13.** It uses identity rows rendered with thinking OFF, plus 10% of thinking-ON identity rows with GLM reasoning, plus the thinking-ON tool-calling replay rows doubled.
  - BFCL 28.3%: +0.7 points [−3.4, +4.4] vs v0.1.
  - With thinking ON, its final answer gives the name in 35 and the creator in 32 of 52 core identity prompts, and it never claims another lab.
  - GSM8K is −1.1 [−1.9, −0.3]; MATH500 is unchanged.
- **Fallback: A3** (identity rows with thinking OFF only). It has the best BFCL (31.1%), but its reasoning often invents a "system message", and GSM8K is −1.7 [−2.6, −0.9].
- **Merging A3 and A8a does not combine their strengths.** BFCL and the reasoning quirk switch together near t = 0.5.
- **Every 36-update recipe costs about 1–2 points of GSM8K.** Halving the training removes that cost but collapses BFCL.
- Our earlier "thinking-ON format broken" counts were mostly a parser artefact. With special tokens kept, the models open and close their thinking like v0.1.

## Setup

- **Start:** Snowball v0.1. Learning rate 2e-6 constant, global batch 8 × 8192 tokens, seed 310. Router, Q/K, biases and 256 special-token rows are frozen in every arm unless noted.
- **Identity data:** Held's set after capping the "not known / should not guess" refusal rows. Thinking-ON rows with reasoning use QC-passed GLM rationales.
- **Replay:** v0.1's own answers on chat, maths, code and tool-calling prompts.
- **Evals:**
  - **BFCL parity:** 123 tasks, Pi 0.87.0 agent. Five full runs per model, with a run-level bootstrap. Pi sends no temperature, so the server default (1.0) applies.
  - **Identity check:** 52 core identity prompts + 14 third-person controls, thinking OFF and ON, no system prompt, read with special tokens kept.
  - **Maths:** paired GSM8K (thinking OFF) and MATH500 (thinking ON), 3 decodes each.
  - **SWE100:** mini-swe-agent 2.1.

## BFCL (5 full runs unless noted)

| Arm | What changed | BFCL | vs v0.1 [95% CI] |
|---|---|---:|---|
| v0.1 | — | 27.6% | — |
| A0 | identity rows; thinking-ON rows have empty thinking | 15.6% | −12.1 [−16.5, −7.6] |
| A1 | A0 without the special-token freeze | 14.8% | −12.8 [−16.3, −9.9] |
| A2 | replay only | 24.6% | −3.1 [−6.2, −0.7] |
| A3 | identity rows rendered thinking OFF only | 31.1% | +3.4 [−0.5, +7.2] |
| A4 | earlier CD16-T3 recipe, 36 updates | 36.3% | +8.6 [+4.4, +11.9] |
| A6 | thinking-ON rows with GLM reasoning (1,791 rows) | 15.4% | −12.2 [−15.6, −9.3] |
| A8b | A3 + 30% of A6's thinking-ON rows (537) | 17.2% | −10.4 [−14.0, −7.3] |
| A8a | A3 + 10% of A6's thinking-ON rows (179) | 26.2% | −1.5 [−4.9, +1.5] |
| A9 | A8a, 72 updates | 24.6% | −3.1 [−6.7, +0.3] |
| A10 | Tülu-style: 44 identity Q&As × 10 | 24.0% | −3.7 [−8.0, +0.0] (4 runs) |
| A11 | A3, 72 updates | 31.2% | +3.6 [−0.5, +7.5] |
| A12 | A8a, first 18 updates | 14.8% | −12.8 [−16.4, −9.9] |
| **A13** | **A8a + thinking-ON tool replay doubled** | **28.3%** | **+0.7 [−3.4, +4.4]** |
| M25 | 0.75·A3 + 0.25·A8a | 30.4% | +2.8 [−0.8, +6.0] |
| M49 | 0.51·A3 + 0.49·A8a | 29.5% | +1.8 [−1.7, +4.9] (4 runs) |
| M51 | 0.49·A3 + 0.51·A8a | 23.8% | −3.9 [−7.9, +0.1] (4 runs) |
| M75 | 0.25·A3 + 0.75·A8a | 23.9% | −3.7 [−6.8, −1.3] |

How the failing models fail (first registered run, 123 tasks):

| | A0 | A3 | A6 | A8a | A8b | A9 | A10 | A12 | A13 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Answers once, no tool call | 60 | 12 | 66 | 17 | 43 | 40 | 44 | 45 | 16 |
| Recites its identity in a tool task | 3 | 0 | 29 | 0 | 15 | 1 | 0 | 3 | 1 |

## Identity (special tokens kept, no system prompt)

Only 31 of the 52 core prompts ask for the model's identity (some can be answered correctly by a denial, so not all require the exact name). 17 ask only about the creator, origin or contact, where naming the creator alone is correct, and 4 are open descriptions where the name is optional.

| Model | Thinking ON: name / creator / claims another lab (of 52) | Thinking OFF: name / creator / other lab | Reasoning invents a system message (of 52) | Rewrites another lab's fact (of 14), OFF / ON |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| v0.1 | 0 / 0 / 46 | 0 / 0 / 41 | 10 | 0 / 0 |
| A3 | 31 / 44 / 0 | 30 / 34 / 0 | 17 | 0 / 0 |
| A8a | 34 / 33 / 0 | 29 / 30 / 1 | 1 | 0 / 0 |
| **A13** | **35 / 32 / 0** | **29 / 30 / 1** | **3** | **0 / 0** |
| A9 | 32 / 40 / 1 | 28 / 39 / 1 | 1 | 1 / 1 |
| A10 | 26 / 32 / 9 | 29 / 24 / 5 | 3 | 0 / 0 |
| A11 | 31 / 37 / 2 | 27 / 39 / 1 | 16 | 1 / 1 |
| A12 | 30 / 33 / 1 | 31 / 35 / 3 | 0 | 0 / 0 |
| M25 | 32 / 45 / 0 | 29 / 33 / 0 | 18 | 0 / 0 |
| M49 | 30 / 40 / 0 | 29 / 32 / 0 | 13 | 0 / 0 |
| M51 | 33 / 31 / 0 | 30 / 30 / 0 | 1 | 0 / 0 |
| M75 | 33 / 34 / 0 | 30 / 30 / 0 | 1 | 0 / 0 |

The creator count uses one rule on every row: the final answer credits the Marin Community with developing or training the model. Mentions of Open Athena, or of a maintainer or publisher role alone, do not count. Thinking-ON answers are read after the model's own end-of-thinking token.

## Maths (paired against v0.1, 3 decodes)

v0.1 scores 92.1% on GSM8K and 92.0% on MATH500. Our pre-set stop line is a drop of more than 1.5 points with the whole interval below zero.

| Model | GSM8K (thinking OFF) | MATH500 (thinking ON) |
|---|---|---|
| A3 | −1.7 [−2.6, −0.9] (stop) | −0.2 [−1.4, +1.0] |
| A8a | −1.1 [−1.9, −0.3] | +0.7 [−0.5, +1.9] |
| A11 | −1.3 [−2.1, −0.5] | −0.3 [−1.4, +0.9] |
| A12 | +0.2 [−0.7, +1.1] | +0.1 [−1.0, +1.1] |
| **A13** | **−1.1 [−1.9, −0.3]** | unchanged |
| M25 | −1.5 [−2.4, −0.7] (stop) | unchanged |
| M49 | −1.6 [−2.5, −0.8] (stop) | unchanged |
| M51 | −1.2 [−2.0, −0.4] | +0.9 [−0.2, +2.0] |
| M75 | −1.2 [−2.1, −0.4] | unchanged |

## SWE100 (mini-swe-agent 2.1, full 100/100 runs only)

| Model | Runs | Mean | vs v0.1 [95% CI] |
|---|---|---:|---|
| v0.1 | 28, 33, 28 | 29.7% | — |
| A0 | 28 | 28.0% | 1 run, no interval |
| A3 | 28, 29, 28 | 28.3% | −1.3 [−4.7, +0.7] |
| A8a | 25, 27, 28, 29 | 27.3% | −2.4 [−5.6, +0.2] |

- **No BFCL-size collapse here, even for A0.** mini-swe-agent re-prompts any reply without a command, so the model cannot simply answer and stop. Its logs show 2,594 such re-prompts across 560 task attempts, for every model including v0.1.
- **SWE100 is not sensitive to this failure.**
- **Preemptions** left A0 with one full run.

## Ben's identity panel (Panel-60)

Ben's 60-question identity/history panel, run with his protocol (thinking off, temperature 0). One model grader graded all 300 answers blind and shuffled. Any Marin-family name counts as correct. Ship line: clean ≥ 20, name ≥ 15, claims another lab ≤ 3.

| Model | Clean | Name = Marin | Creator = Marin | Claims another lab | Invents facts |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| v0.1 | 10 | 5 | 4 | 17 | 22 |
| v0.1 + system prompt | 33 | 26 | 40 | 4 | 13 |
| **A13** | 15 | **35** | 54 | **1** | 3 |
| A8a | 14 | 35 | 47 | 0 | 3 |
| A3 | 15 | 34 | 56 | 0 | 1 |

- **Identity:** all three pass the name and other-lab lines by a wide margin.
- **Clean:** all three miss it. The grader's reasons are about answer quality, not identity. The models recite a canned identity line instead of answering the question asked, or don't explain how the model relates to the Marin project.
- **Grading note:** the grader was told that item 26 holds A3's length-terminated answer, which identifies A3's answer on that item. All other items are label-blind. A3's counts are unchanged without item 26.

## Mini840 (in progress)

We tried Mini840 (#10804) on the top candidates. The published runtime cannot run its own suite as is.

- **The agentic tasks need a pre-built environment snapshot map, which was not published.** We built our own Daytona snapshots. A key bug (the key depends on folder permissions) broke DS-1000. That is fixed, and a fixed pilot is running.
- **The non-agentic graders request CPU and storage that the published local grader refuses,** so every non-agentic grading row fails. OlympiadBench's judge address is also empty.
- No Mini840 scores yet.

## Training length vs tool-example dose

A12 is not a low tool-calling dose; it is A8a stopped halfway (18 of 36 updates). The two kinds of "more" behave differently:

| What increased | Arms | BFCL |
|---|---|---|
| Training length (same mix) | A12 (18) → A8a (36) → A9 (72) | 14.8% → 26.2% → 24.6% |
| Thinking-ON tool replay | A8a (1×) → A13 (2×) | 26.2% → 28.3% (+2.1 [−1.5, +5.7]) |

- Tool calling drops early in training and recovers by update 36; more training of the same mix does not improve it further.
- More thinking-ON examples that end in a tool call help a little, consistent with the "answer and stop" mechanism. Not tested beyond 2×.

## What did not work

- **Context distillation from v0.1 with an identity system prompt,** for thinking-ON rows: 0 of 200 pilot traces passed QC, even with an instruction not to mention the system prompt.
- **A3 with a forced thinking start as the teacher:** 11 of 200 passed QC.
- **More training** (A9, A11): no identity gain, plus a few other-lab rewrites (for example, "GPT-4 trained by the Marin Community").
- **Less training** (A12): tool calling collapses. It breaks early and recovers by update 36.
- **A tiny Tülu-style set** (A10): weaker identity; it still claims another lab in 9 of 52 thinking-ON answers.
- **Linear merges of A3 and A8a:** no blend gets both A3's BFCL and A8a's clean reasoning.

## Models

A3, A8a and A13 are archived in public HF repos under open-athena, with recipe, data hashes and scores in each card:

- `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A3-2026.10.30`
- `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A8a-2026.10.30`
- `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A13-2026.10.30`

issues.author: karansag
issues.body: ## TL;DR (Conclusion) **Final, 2026-10-24: stopped and written up.** No SFT method beat plain SFT by enough to matter; the source of the traces decided the result. See the [summary comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10213#issuecomment-6618401658) and the [paper](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/f0ad30e1ebafa432c3af144aa6faad76119a6c97/logbooks/10213-sft-shootout/agentic-sft-shootout.pdf). The design-stage text below is kept as written. Design stage, 2026-10-16. We compare five supervised fine-tuning (SFT) mechanisms for agentic coding on one base, one task pool, one teacher and one supervised-token budget: plain SFT (one accepted demonstration per task), rejection-sampled SFT with resampling across epochs, relay SFT (#10027), recovery SFT, and plateau dropping (#10028). The earlier transfer experiments (#9920, #9984) compared plain SFT, rejection-sampled SFT, on-policy distillation and weight merging on non-agentic tasks; this experiment moves to agentic tasks under the eval policy (#10197) and drops merging and distillation. Nothing has trained yet except a learning-rate sweep of the control, which is in progress. ## Question Which mechanism, if any, improves Snowball v0 on SWE-bench Verified and the terminal benchmarks over plain SFT at equal supervised tokens, without losing retention on GSM8K, BFCL-Parity and GPQA-Diamond. ## Fixed choices - Base: Snowball v0 = `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign3-DARE-Linear-02-2026.10.12` @ `4eeb756b`. v0 carries a diluted DARE graft of the allkimi relay SFT, so relay's lift reads smaller than it would on a pre-graft checkpoint; this is accepted because the question is what improves the release. - Task pool: about 2,200 TMax environments (`allenai/TMax-SFT-16.5K`, tasks.zip) and about 2,100 SWE-smith tasks sampled from the Harbor packages in `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s`, stratified by repository, SWE-bench Verified repositories removed, decontaminated through DataKit against SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and TBLite 2.0. Selection is outcome-blind. SWE-smith packages receive a git-history strip before the agent phase (#10212). - Harness per task family, matching the policy's scoring agent: TMax under Terminus-2, SWE-smith under mini-swe-agent 2.1.0, both in Harbor under the policy pins. - Teacher: GLM 5.3 through the internal inference service, 8 attempts per task, verified by each task's tests. v0 is never sampled except in relay, where it starts each task and GLM continues after a trigger (format error, context budget, completion claim). - Recipe, shared by every arm: the #9984 comparison-arm settings (AdamW, betas 0.9/0.999, weight decay 0, clip 1.0, router bias frozen, batch 16 at 32k context, constant learning rate, loss averaged over supervised tokens), 3 epochs, replay of general SFT data (`nemotron_sft_v3`, reasoning kept) at one quarter of the agentic budget. The learning rate comes from the sweep below. ## Arms and token matching B is the supervised-token count of the plain arm: the first passing attempt per task with at least one pass, one trajectory per task. Every arm trains on B agentic tokens plus the same replay slice for the same number of optimizer steps. - Plain SFT (control): as above. - RS-multi: identical task slots to plain; when a task recurs in a later epoch, a different passing attempt is used. Measures demonstration diversity at a fixed budget. - Relay (#10027): v0's own turns stay in context with no loss; GLM's turns are trained; passing episodes subsampled to B. Episodes with no teacher turn are dropped. - Recovery (phase 2): the plain trajectories; 20% receive one or two synthetic failed turns re-rendered in v0's measured error styles plus the real harness error, inserted through the parser; injections carry no loss, so the budget equals B by construction. Waits on a validated injection generator. - Plateau dropping (#10028, phase 2): the plain trajectories; tokens whose loss has plateaued lose gradient; matched on optimizer steps, with gradient-carrying tokens reported. Waits on the trainer. Phase 1 is plain, RS-multi and relay. ## Evaluation Every arm, including plain, runs the retention gate (GSM8K, BFCL-Parity, GPQA-Diamond) and the agentic endpoint (SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1, TBLite 2.0) under the policy's trial counts and pins. An arm passes when it has no decisive loss against plain on the gate and a decisive win over plain on at least one agentic benchmark with no decisive loss on the others, where decisive is the policy's rule (gap above 1.96 times the combined task-level standard error, each scaled by 1/sqrt(0.9)). One policy run resolves gaps of roughly 4 to 5 points on SWE-bench Verified and 8 to 10 on the terminal benchmarks; unresolved arms are reported with intervals and not promoted. Passing arms, plain and v0 go to the 23-benchmark tournament. ## Learning-rate sweep of the control Running now, on pilot data (existing Qwen3.6-27B TMax traces and Kimi-2.5 SWE-smith traces, history-reading trials removed), four runs from v0 at 3e-7, 1e-6, 3e-6 and 1e-5, 3 epochs, recipe otherwise fixed. Screens per run: held-out validation loss on 5% of tasks, GSM8K, BFCL-Parity, SWE-bench Verified random-100 and a 100-task TBLite subset. Decision rule, fixed in advance: among rates with no decisive retention loss against v0, the best equal-weight mean of the two agentic screens; ties to the smaller rate. The chosen rate is confirmed once on the real plain-arm data and then frozen for all arms. ## Budget Core (sweep, generation, phase 1, tournament) about 3,700 to 4,000 H100-hours; phase 2 adds about 2,400, of which 1,700 is an optional 20-epoch plateau comparison. GLM generation runs on the internal service and sandbox CPU and is outside the GPU budget. ## Status and next steps - Pilot dataset and learning-rate sweep: in progress. - Task pool, decontamination and package fix: in progress. - Harness bring-up, one-task dry runs, a 200-task-per-family pass-rate pilot and a relay dry run: in progress. The full 8-attempt generation waits on their results. - Then: phase-1 training, first-stage evaluation, tournament for passers; phase 2 when its code exists. Design notes and diagrams are kept in the maintainer's notes and will be attached as results land. ## Decision log - 2026-10-15: scope cut to SFT only; merging and on-policy distillation dropped. Base set to Snowball v0. - 2026-10-16: one harness per task family following the policy's scoring agents; GLM 5.3 as the single teacher with regenerated traces instead of reusing Kimi and Qwen traces; RS arm redefined as resampling across epochs after the token-budgeted variant was found to re-weight tasks; task eligibility defined by teacher success only; unfiltered-SFT control dropped; primary endpoint set to the agentic benchmarks with the tournament secondary; git-history leak found in the SWE-smith packages and a strip added to the pool build.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Teacher generation bring-up: one-task dry runs

## TL;DR

GLM 5.3 now runs end to end in both harnesses (Harbor `016dd78b`, Daytona sandboxes, run from cw-us-east-02a):
- TMax under Terminus-2, with the 65,536 / 16,384 limits from the policy;
- SWE-smith under the mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 adapter, with a 32,768-token window.

**The adapter question is answered.** The mini-swe-agent adapter runs a raw SWE-smith Harbor package unchanged, and the dry-run trace fit inside 32k (largest prompt 13.4k tokens). One trace says nothing about the length distribution; the pilot will measure it.

**The GLM pass on SWE-smith read the fix from git history** (#10212). Before the SWE-smith pass-rate pilot, the packages need the history-stripped repair.

**The pilot has not started.** It waits on a capacity confirmation for the GLM service.

## Per trial

| | TMax `task_000000_5c5b0938` | SWE-smith `swesmith-00003` |
|---|---|---|
| Reward | 0 in the first run, 1 in a rerun | 1 in both runs |
| Model calls | 4 | 16 to 17 |
| Prompt tokens (total / largest) | 9.3k to 10.1k / 3.7k | 145k to 156k (about 93% prefix-cached) / 13.4k |
| Completion tokens (reasoning) | 5.1k to 6.2k (4.2k to 5.2k) | 3.4k to 3.6k (0.5k to 0.8k) |
| Model time | 39 s | 16 s |
| Trial wall time | 42 to 93 s (environment build 3 to 45 s) | 74 to 80 s (verifier 20 to 25 s) |

## Effective generation settings

Both clients send only `model` and `max_tokens=16384`, so GLM runs on the service defaults. GLM 5.3's template then renders `Reasoning Effort: Max`.

Every request is logged by an in-cluster proxy. The log records the settings as sent and the full reply, reasoning included. The proxy also serves `/tokenize` with the `zai-org/GLM-5.3` tokenizer, because the mini-swe-agent context limiter needs it and the relay does not provide it. Its token counts matched the service on every request.

## Transcripts

Both harnesses write Harbor ATIF trajectories:
- **Terminus-2:** each step's message is the JSON action, and the reasoning is in `reasoning_content`.
- **mini-swe-agent:** native `bash` tool calls with `{returncode, output}` observations, but the trajectory **drops GLM's reasoning**. Training rows are therefore rebuilt from the proxy log, which keeps it. That rebuild checks clean on both dry runs.

## What the agent can see

Measured with an oracle-agent probe during the agent phase:

| | TMax (converted) | SWE-smith (raw package) |
|---|---|---|
| `/tests` | absent | absent |
| `/solution` | absent | absent |
| Other task files | none | none |
| Git history | no repository | 944 branches, including `main` and the full history |

The SWE-smith dry-run pass used that history: it ran `git show 614b134:<file>`, then checked its edit against that file. Details are in #10212.

## Other findings

- **TMax is not in Harbor format** in `tasks.zip`. The pool converts it with TMax's own `convert_to_harbor.py` at `hamishivi/tmax@6d3d606c`, minus 181 environments with hidden verifier assets, giving 2,019 tasks.
- **The dry-run TMax task looks flawed.** It runs an OpenMP parallel loop over the outer LU loop with 4 threads, while the test expects the sequential determinant. The task failed once and passed once.

## Next

- **TMax pilot:** 200 tasks x 2 attempts, seed 20261016, drawn uniformly from 1,963 eligible tasks (the pool minus #202's held-out ids). Staged; starts when capacity is confirmed.
- **SWE-smith pilot:** 200 x 2, stratified by repository, on the history-stripped packages.
- **Relay dry run:** 20 tasks per family, with v0 served by the policy serving config. GLM takes over on these triggers:
  - format error: GLM writes one repair turn;
  - context budget at 0.75 of the window: GLM continues to the end;
  - completion claim: v0's reply is withheld and logged, and GLM continues to the end.

Run folders: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/generation/dryrun/{tmax-dry1,tmax-dry2,swe-dry3,swe-dry4,visibility1}`

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Relay rounds broken by a preempted student server ([#10237](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10237)).

**Affected rounds**
- TMax relay shard-02 round 1: 198 of 200 trials errored, 14:33-15:13 UTC on 2026-10-17. Moved to `traces/tmax-relay/shard-02/round-1.failed-0a6b03ad`; it will be rerun. It was never published.
- SWE-smith relay shard-00 round 3: 85 of 97 trials errored, from about 08:29 UTC. Its 32 valid rows are published; trials that raised without a GLM reply don't count as relay runs.

I'm checking every other round for a student preemption and will post the full list.

**Cause.** In relay mode, the v0 student runs as a child inference job. When that job was preempted, Iris rescheduled it on another host. The relay proxy kept calling the address resolved once at startup (`lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris.py:682`). Every student call then failed with `httpx.ConnectError`, the agents got HTTP 500, and Harbor still exited 0.

**Fix** (`task/212` @ [`174906474a`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/174906474a8039d1ff8989e8f6d53103242cfec1)):
- On a connection error, the proxy looks up the student's current address and retries for up to 20 minutes.
- The proxy logs its own failures, which used to go unlogged.
- A run fails, with no `_SUCCESS`, when more than 20% of its trials raise without a reply.

The relay lanes are being resubmitted on this commit.

🤖 Decisions for the next data round (v7), 2026-10-19.

1. Regenerate the GLM 5.3 pool at a lower reasoning effort. The max-effort traces caused both phase-1 defects: long reasoning used up the 30k generation window (so half of the passing SWE-smith attempts never reached the submit step) and taught a style that times out TBLite. GLM 5.3's chat template exposes only `low`, `high` and max (`medium` renders as max, and `high` reasoned to the token cap like max in a probe), so a pilot of 200 TMax and 200 SWE-smith tasks x 2 samples at `low` and `high` is running (launched 21:01 UTC) to measure pass rate, clean-pass rate, per-turn reasoning and context use against the max-effort pool. The full k=8 regeneration on pool v5, plus relay rounds, follows at the chosen setting with the same gates.
2. Select demonstrations by clean completion: an attempt counts only if it passed and ended with the agent's own finish (mini-swe-agent submit, Terminus-2 `task_complete`). On the max-effort traces this keeps 919 of 1,995 SWE-smith tasks and 1,475 of 1,914 TMax tasks; the lower-effort traces should keep more.
3. Switch the base to Snowball v0.1 (`open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14`, selected in #10283 under the same policy). Same architecture, tokenizer and template as v0, and without v0's relay SFT graft, so it is a cleaner base for the relay arm. The relay student becomes v0.1 and v0.1 reference screens will be run. The LR sweep result (1e-6, 3 epochs) is carried over rather than repeated.
4. Rebuild all five arms on the new rows, retrain and screen them. The v5 arms above remain the max-effort finding.

Recovery SFT implementation check: the owner obtained the original recovery generation code; the mechanism matches ours (injection points, 1–3 attempts, Terminus-2 reply template and parser, teacher-authored failed turns, masking). Two rendering details from it are adopted (varied renders per error style; streaks of the same style, with rates measured on v0's own trajectories: 56.6% same style, 0% identical); we keep trained tokens equal to plain's.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 **Update 2026-10-22: every SFT arm trained on the GLM 5.3 traces scores below its parent on the agentic screens. Two next steps: re-run the cheap arms on the contributor (Kimi/Qwen) traces, and check the learning rate on the real rows.**

## Results on the GLM 5.3 traces

Screens are SWE-bench Verified random-100 and the TBLite 100-task subset (solved out of 100; TBLite timeouts count as failures), GSM8K and BFCL-Parity for retention. "Composite" is our screening mean (SWE + TBLite)/2, shown as a range when trials were unscored for infrastructure reasons; it is a bound, not a confidence interval. HIGH and LOW are the GLM reasoning-effort settings used to generate the traces; rows are token-matched per arm.

| model | parent | rows | SWE-bench r100 (submits) | TBLite-100 | GSM8K | BFCL | composite | EvalDash |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| --- |
| parent v0.1 | – | – | 26 (36) | 23 | 91.1 | 32/123 | 24.5-25.0 |  |
| plain | v0.1 | HIGH | 13 (4) | 8 | 92.3 | 67/123 | 10.5-11.5 |  |
| plain | v0.1 | LOW | 17 (27) | 12 | 91.7 | 55/121 | 14.5-18.0 | [EvalDash](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs?model=v7-plain-low-v01-20261020) |
| relay | v0.1 | LOW | 25 (25) | 15 | 92.9 | 64/123 | 20.0-21.0 | [EvalDash](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs?model=v7-relay-low-v01-20261021) |
| parent v0 | – | – | 33 (56) | 20 | 85.2 | 27/122 | 26.5-27.0 |  |
| plain | v0 | HIGH | 17 (3) | 9 | 87.7 | 44/122 | 13.0-17.5 |  |
| plain, cut to the relay arm's token count | v0 | HIGH | 13 (6) | 11 | 91.1 | 54/123 | 12.0-12.5 |  |
| RS-multi | v0 | HIGH | 11 (6) | 10 | 89.9 | 41/123 | 10.5-11.0 | [EvalDash](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs?model=v7-rs-multi-v0-20261021) |
| recovery | v0 | HIGH | 12 (4) | 9 | 88.5 | 48/123 | 10.5-11.0 | [EvalDash](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs?model=v7-recovery-v0-20261021) |
| relay | v0 | HIGH | 13 (1) | 14 | 89.0 | 48/123 | 13.5-14.0 |  |
| plateau dropping | v0 | HIGH | 14 (6) | 13 | 89.8 | 49/123 | 13.5 |  |

What the data say:
- Every arm is below its parent on SWE-bench and TBLite and above it on GSM8K and BFCL. The regression is specific to the agentic tasks.
- Paired per-task differences on the frozen task lists (task bootstrap, 95%): no HIGH-row method differs from plain on either screen (SWE-bench -3 to -6 [about -13, +4]; TBLite 0 to +3 [about -6, +9]). Relay on the LOW rows beats plain on the LOW rows on SWE-bench by +8 [+1, +16], the only method-versus-twin interval that excludes zero; on TBLite +1 [-6, +7]. Every student is below its parent on SWE-bench (HIGH-row arms -13 to -22, intervals exclude zero; LOW relay -1 [-10, +8]) and most are below on TBLite.
- Relay on the LOW rows is therefore the strongest arm (25 SWE-bench vs the parent's 26), with the caveat that its recipe differs from plain's (963 vs 675 updates at equal tokens, student prefix masked) and that LOW rows hold 11.6M supervised tokens per epoch against HIGH's 19.4M.
- Mechanism, measured on trajectories: students keep the rows' per-step style (about 120 tokens per step, same command mix) but take about twice the rows' steps, run into the 32k window (75-97% of episodes) and rarely submit (HIGH-trained 3-6%, LOW-trained about 25%, parents 36-56%). Submitting is where the score comes from.
- The two parents are not distinguishable on the frozen task lists: paired SWE-bench difference v0 minus v0.1 = +7 [-2, +16], TBLite -3 [-12, +6] (task bootstrap). Of the 49 TBLite tasks where v0.1 timed out, v0 solved 3, so v0.1's timeouts are mostly hard tasks, not lost score (#10338: tripling the limit changed its score by one task).

Limits: one run per arm, 100 tasks per screen (about 4 points of standard error), TBLite timeout-bound for every student.

## Next step 1: the same cheap arms on the contributor traces

The one run of this recipe that beat its parent was the learning-rate sweep's 1e-6 run on the pilot traces (Qwen3.6-27B TMax episodes and Kimi-2.5 SWE-smith episodes, the data the contributors' original experiments used): composite 31.0-32.0 against v0's 26.5-27.0, TBLite 29 vs 20. That run used the sweep's sampler and exposure, not the arm recipe, so it is suggestive, not a control. The pilot rows also look different from the GLM rows: 14 steps per episode at 246 tokens per step with 28% reasoning tokens (HIGH: 25 steps, 120 tokens, 39%), and they are in Terminus-2 format, which never contains the mini-swe-agent submit command, yet that student kept 40% submits.

Plan: convert the pilot traces to the arm row format and train plain, RS-multi and recovery from v0.1 at 1e-6 under the arm recipe, plus plain from v0 as the bridge to the sweep. v0.1 is the base because it carries no relay graft and v0 was trained on about half of the pilot SWE tasks through the relay data grafted into it. Known limits: the Kimi SWE set has one trajectory per task, so RS-multi runs on TMax only; recovery needs an error style for Qwen's native tool calls; about 1,500 pilot SWE tasks have only the pilot's own decontamination check. Target: plain results within a day of the rows, the other two a day later.

## Next step 2: learning rate on the real rows

The sweep tied 3e-7, 1e-6 and 3e-6 on the pilot rows and 1e-6 was frozen without the planned confirmation on real plain rows. Two checks are running: plain SFT on the LOW v0 rows at 3e-7, paired against the 1e-6 twin (same rows, parent and schedule), to test whether gentler updates preserve more of the parent; and a screen of the HIGH plain v0.1 epoch-2 checkpoint against its final, as an update-dose check. A higher rate is not excluded but is the less likely direction given the sweep.

Also in flight: plain, relay and plateau on the LOW rows from v0, and RS-multi and recovery on the LOW rows from v0.1, to complete the LOW comparison on both parents. Models so far are on the Hub under `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-SFT-Shootout-*` (private). Design: [SFT comparison doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/13duCN6reb7KVLhBi8TszTL1EYKeaV3SEMQhl9IJCZSM/edit).

Paired per-task differences (task bootstrap, 95%):

| comparison | SWE-bench | TBLite |

| contribshared − lowshared (the matched pair) | **+26 [+17, +36]** | **+9 [+1, +17]** |

What the data say:
- On identical tasks, GLM LOW rows push the student far below the parent, and contributor rows lift it above the parent on SWE-bench. The contributor-side +10 is the first gap against the parent that clears noise.

A lower learning rate (3e-7: SWE −7 [−13, −1] against 1e-6) and an earlier checkpoint (2 of 3 epochs: +5 [−4, +13]) also did not rescue the GLM rows.

Not tested: what remains between the row sets is the teacher (GLM 5.3 against Kimi/Qwen) and the harness format. Our GLM rows use each eval's own action protocol; the contributor rows use the other one.

Trace decontamination: the trained trace text was checked against the 100 SWE-bench gold and test patches and the 100 TBLite tests and solutions. There were 3 flags, all TBLite, all generic code (imports, a file-reading loop). Nothing was excluded.

Cost of these runs: 184.9 H100-h training and 106.4 H100-h screens. Documented total for the experiment: about 6,070 H100-h (a partial subtotal, not an invoice).

comments.author: karansag
comments.body: 🤖 **Summary: no SFT method beat plain SFT by enough to matter; the source of the traces decided the result. The experiment is stopped and written up.** ## Data We took 2,200 TMAX and 2,100 SWE-smith tasks and regenerated traces using GLM 5.3. This way, both would have a consistent teacher. We also ran these traces using the corresponding eval harness under policy. For SWE-smith, this was `mini-swe-agent`, and for TMax, it was `Terminus-2`. Relay pools were also constructed similarly, starting with a base Snowball and handing off to GLM 5.3 Note that GLM 5.3 was tried with different effort levels (as per comments above). We used the contributor rows directly (SWE-smith + TMax under Kimi 2.5 / Qwen3.6-27B) for both pilot sweeps and as a final run to assess the impact of our data after a negative with GLM 5.3 traces. ## What we did We compared plain SFT, rejection-sampled SFT (RS-multi), relay, recovery and plateau dropping for agentic coding on Snowball v0 and v0.1. The task pool was about 2,200 TMax and 2,100 SWE-smith tasks. Traces came from GLM 5.3 at three reasoning efforts, then from the contributor traces (Kimi-2.5 SWE-smith, Qwen3.6-27B TMax). Screens: SWE-bench Verified random-100, TBLite-100, GSM8K and BFCL-Parity. ## What we found 1. **Every arm trained on GLM 5.3 traces scored below its parent** on SWE-bench and TBLite, while gaining on GSM8K and BFCL. The students took about twice the steps of their training traces, ran into the 32k context limit in most SWE-bench episodes and rarely submitted. 2. **Methods mattered little.** Only relay on LOW rows beat plain SFT (SWE-bench +8 [+1, +16]), and it still trailed its parent. On contributor rows, plain, RS-multi, recovery and plateau dropping were indistinguishable. 3. **The rows mattered most.** With the same 1,432 tasks, parent and recipe, contributor rows beat GLM LOW rows by SWE-bench +26 [+17, +36] and TBLite +9 [+1, +17]. The contributor side also beat parent v0.1 on SWE-bench by +10 [+1, +19]. 4. **Less GLM exposure did not help.** A lower learning rate, an earlier checkpoint and a smaller subset all stayed below the parent. ## Hypotheses (untested) Why the GLM arms lost while the contributor rows gained, and why collaborators got large SFT gains from Kimi and Qwen traces on a weaker Snowball parent ([blog post, 2026-10-21](https://lukedhlee.github.io/blog/2026/10/21/turning-snowball-into-a-coding-agent/)). Ordered by how much evidence we have. 1. **Teacher traces.** GLM 5.3 episodes were long, reasoning-heavy and often ended at the context limit; the students copied that. Kimi and Qwen traces did not. The matched pair (+26 SWE-bench on the same tasks) is the strongest evidence we have for anything. A different teacher on the same tasks and format would test it. 2. **SFT alone does not fix action behavior.** The collaborators' best results came from SFT then RL; their trace analysis found RL cut invalid actions from about 80% to 2% and taught the model to submit its best effort instead of running out of context. Those are exactly the failures of our GLM students. RL from a shootout checkpoint would test it. 3. **Training stack.** The collaborators report that an early relay advantage disappeared after correcting training precision and MoE expert capacity. Our arms trained before #10492 made expert capacity configurable; at the default capacity with expert parallelism, overflow tokens are dropped silently (seen later in the identity work). Whether the shootout arms dropped tokens is not known. It can be checked by replaying one saved run with drop counting. 4. **Eval protocol.** Our screens use 32k context, 1,800 s and one trial; the collaborators use 64k, a 3x timeout and three repeats. Our GLM students produce longer episodes, so our limits may punish them more than a longer protocol would. The 65k-context and 5,400 s checks ran on the parent only, not on a student. 5. **Parent headroom.** Their parent was the general-SFT 09-21 checkpoint (12.8% SWE-bench under Terminus-2). Ours were merged and RL-trained parents, and v0 already carries a relay graft trained on 1,012 of the same Kimi trajectories. Demonstrations may have less to add to our parents. 6. **Harness format.** Our GLM traces were recorded in each eval's own harness and hurt that eval; the contributor traces were recorded the other way round and did not. Training in the eval's own format may overwrite the parent's behavior there. But the collaborators' Kimi SWE traces are Terminus-2 format and their SWE eval runs under Terminus-2, and that worked, so this is weaker than it first looked. Format is confounded with the teacher. Re-recording GLM traces in the other format (about 125 H100-h) would separate them. 7. **Training dose.** We trained 3 epochs at 1e-6. The collaborators' RL started from a 7-epoch SFT model, and their RL ablation found more epochs helped until overfitting. This would not rescue the GLM arms, which got worse, but the contributor rows were never trained past 3 epochs. spillover_issues.author: davidlundgren
spillover_issues.body:
🤖

Every RL turn passes through [`DirectModelClient._generate_chat`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3ae74d9560/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/trajectory_runners/model_clients.py#L296-L301). That method already decodes the exact response tokens with special tokens kept, then calls `final_answer_text`. `<|start_think|>` and `<|end_think|>` are single special tokens, so a check on the decoded text sees the same span boundaries as a check on token IDs. The fix changes only vendored SkyRL code. `rolloutengine` and `ModelTurn` stay the same.

1. In `answer_extraction.py`, add `reasoning_span_violation(text) -> ReasoningViolation | None`. `ReasoningViolation` is a `StrEnum` with the values `UNCLOSED`, `SECOND_SPAN`, and `STRAY_END`. When the text has a violation, `final_answer_text` returns `""`, so `<|start_think|>A<|end_think|>B<|end_think|>C` no longer grades as `C`.
2. In `_generate_chat`, when the response has a violation, clear `tool_calls` and `content` so that no tool call runs, and record the violation in the turn's `metadata`. The sampled tokens and log probabilities stay the same.
3. In `task_worker.py`, if any turn of a rollout has a violation, grade it as `Outcome.SUBMISSION_FAILURE` with reward 0. This also covers a SWE rollout that fixed the repo in earlier turns and then produced a malformed turn.
4. Tests: one parser case for each violation, one transport case that shows the tool call is dropped, and one rollout whose earlier turn is malformed but whose final answer is correct (expected reward 0).

These parts of the done-when list are deferred:
- the missing-span and `/nothink`-span checks, which depend on #10519
- the Baby RSI transport, on #9626
- the thinking-enabled probe, on #10399

`has_reasoning_format_violation` stays unchanged. It reproduces NVIDIA's penalty for plain-text `<think>` tags, and step 1 covers the special-token markers.

spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body:
## TL;DR

We measured what new base models already know about the chat assistant format. We also measured what post-training changes. The full report is at [What's in a base?](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/benjaminfeuer/whats-in-a-base/2026.11.05/index.html).

The Qwen3.5-35B-A3B base gives the chat scaffold and two tool-call formats low perplexity (2.0 to 6.5) with no context. It gets 0.73 on BFCL without post-training. Post-training changes few positions, but it changes them strongly: the think tag, the tool-call format after an instruction, and the start of a response. The main cause of the base's agentic failures was that it did not stop at its end-of-turn token. With `<|im_end|>` as a stop token, its SWE-bench Verified score increased from 0.05 to 0.55, higher than its Terminus SFT (0.32). The number of verified SWE-bench rows also changed (20 to 40), and the SFT ran under Pi, not its trained Terminus protocol. BFCL decreased from 0.73 to 0.63, and CRUXEval increased from 0.50 to 0.81.

Post-trained Qwen gives lower probability to text from other assistants. With controlled decode settings, this penalty under post-trained Qwen3.5 is about half as large, and for GLM-4.7-Flash it is zero. Most of the large penalty on the Marin 67B A2B Snowball SFT came from how its traces were sampled. The pinned Evalchemy removed `temperature` from local chat requests. The checkpoint had no sampling defaults, so vLLM sampled at temperature 1.0 without truncation. Mini840 sets sampling explicitly, so this problem does not affect the Mini840 scores.

## Description

We used three methods:

1. **Probes.** We scored short strings by teacher forcing. The strings were the chat scaffold, tool calls in JSON and XML, the think tag, math, Python code and planted canaries. We scored them with no context and in agent contexts. The models were four Qwen bases, post-trained Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6, and the Snowball base and SFT.
2. **Mini840 evaluations** ([#10804](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10804)), a compact form of the Marin eval policy ([#10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197)). We ran three chat-aligned SFT models, two bases and two Snowball checkpoints, all under version `2026.10.31.150013`. We ran the Qwen3.5 base again with `<|im_end|>` as a stop token ([#10901](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10901)). That run is version `2026.11.04.4`, compared with the original base run `2026.10.31.23`.
3. **Trace likelihood.** Five models scored 100 IFBench responses from each of 11 authors, per token. A decode ablation generated the traces again for five authors at three settings: greedy, the shipped default, and temperature 0.6 with top-p 0.95.

All jobs ran on Iris `cw-rno2a`:
- **Mini840:** the model under test was served on 2 H100s, and a separate judge ran on 8 H100s.
- **Snowball probes, trace scoring and the decode ablation:** vLLM at TP1 × DP4 with expert parallelism, on 4 H100s, with a full 8-H100 node reserved per job. The decode ablation used vLLM `39e62869`, which is newer than the campaign build.
- **Qwen probes:** transformers (sdpa), not vLLM.

## Hypothesis or Goal

New pretraining mixtures contain assistant-format and tool-call data. If so, base models give these formats low perplexity, and post-training changes only a small number of positions.

## Status

Complete. One follow-up has no issue yet: in a separate experiment, Snowball base wrote credential-shaped strings ([#10912](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10912), closed). Nobody has searched the pretraining mixture for these strings.

## Results

| Measurement | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Chat-scaffold perplexity, Qwen2.5-7B → Qwen3.5-35B-A3B base | 178 → 2.0 |
| Think-tag perplexity at the assistant turn, Qwen3.5 base → post-trained (one token, wide error bars) | 793 → 1.0 |
| Snowball `<\|start_think\|>` probability: base / SFT with `Reasoning: /think` | about 1e-22 / 0.999 |
| Lowest no-context canary perplexity in any model (Python code is about 2) | 21 |
| Qwen3.5 base BFCL / Terminus SFT BFCL | 0.73 / 0.07 |
| Qwen3.5 base SWE-bench Verified: no stop → `<\|im_end\|>` stop | 0.05 → 0.55 (verified rows 20 → 40) |
| Qwen3.5 base agentic final turns at the 16,384-token cap | 73 → 39 |
| Qwen3.5 base agentic final outputs with role markers (86 of 451 rows; 80 after the turn-coherence exclusions) | 86 → 0 |
| Qwen3.5 base BFCL / CRUXEval with the stop token | 0.73 → 0.63 / 0.50 → 0.81 |
| Snowball SFT penalty, shipped → greedy (nats/char): post-trained Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6 | +0.052 → +0.027 / +0.026 → +0.019 |
| GLM-4.7-Flash penalty, shipped → greedy (nats/char): post-trained Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6 | +0.024 → +0.000 / +0.016 → +0.004 |

Caveats:
- Each decode-ablation cell is one seeded sample. Its IFBench intervals are about ±0.05.
- In the ablation, the Snowball base received an end-of-turn stop that the checkpoint does not ship with.
- The older Qwen bases used ChatML that we built by hand.

## Reproduction

- **Code:** branch [`benfeuer/whats-in-a-base-repro`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/benfeuer/whats-in-a-base-repro). Start with [`experiments/evaluation/base_model_evals/README.md`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/benfeuer/whats-in-a-base-repro/experiments/evaluation/base_model_evals/README.md). It maps each report section to its code and data.
  - The probe and trace scorer is `experiments/evaluation/mini_policy_runtime/generational_perplexity.py`, with `generational_perplexity_serve.sh`.
  - The stop-token generation config is `experiments/evaluation/mini_policy_runtime/generation-configs/qwen35-35b-a3b-base-im-end-stop/`.
  - Mini840 model pins are in `experiments/evaluation/mini_policy_runtime/cohort.py`. The Hugging Face repository heads moved after these pins, so use the pinned revisions.
  - The analysis scripts are in `experiments/evaluation/base_model_evals/`. They are kept as they ran. Some contain workstation paths and a `secrets.env` credential step, and they do not pass the repository ruff rules.
- **Public data:**
  - [Reports and tables](https://gist.github.com/penfever/2422c4b74ffc7644f282fdc050dfd914): analysis, Mini840 tracker and state log, and the turn-coherence, SFT-improbability, non-greedy, decode-ablation, think-marker and trace-likelihood reports. The state log records the job IDs and most model revisions.
  - [Probe payloads and audits](https://gist.github.com/penfever/c83170094ba051f12694ede515dd83e2): perplexity results for each model, the Snowball think-marker probes, and the Mini840 full-run audits. Each payload file starts with the prefix `JSON_RESULT `. Remove this prefix before you parse the JSON.
  - [IFBench trace set](https://gist.github.com/penfever/3a411b1289e9dbcb8d9edfc36edb8eaf). Two email addresses in model responses are replaced with `[REDACTED-EMAIL]`.
- **Large data:** this data is in Marin-internal object storage, region RNO2A.
  - Mini840 runs: `s3://marin-rno2a/marin/experiments/chat-aligned-base-evals/2026.10.31.150013/`.
  - Stop-token rerun: `s3://marin-rno2a/marin/checkpoints/mini840-e2e-qwen35-35b-a3b-base-im-end-stop/2026.11.04.4`.
  - Per-token trace scores and decode-ablation outputs: `s3://marin-rno2a/marin/experiments/base-model-evals/whats-in-a-base-2026.11.05/`.
- **Models:**
  - Qwen base generations: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B`, `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-Base`, `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base`, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base`. Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen3-8B-Base came from the Hugging Face hub with no recorded revision.
  - Qwen post-trained: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` @ `59d61f3c`, `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` @ `995ad96e`.
  - Snowball base: `open-athena/snowball-67b-a2b-base-262k-qk175-skew8` @ `3bbf729f`.
  - Snowball SFT: `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-Repro-262K-Step471-2026.10.25` @ `51669ee1`. This repository is gated on Hugging Face. Request access before you use it.
  - Mini840 SFT models: `open-athena/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Chat-Aligned-Base-2026.10.31`, `open-athena/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Chat-Aligned-Base-2026.10.30`, `open-athena/Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-Chat-Aligned-Base-2026.10.30` and `laion/snowball-67b-a2b-sft-s3-nemotron-terminal-step1888`. Their pins are in `cohort.py`.
  - Trace authors: the IFBench responses come from the eval-policy campaign. The state log does not record each author's revision.

## Decision Log

- For Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6, we used each model's own chat template, with `enable_thinking=false`. For the older Qwen bases, we used ChatML that we built by hand.
- For both Snowball checkpoints, we used the Snowball SFT chat template.
- The first Snowball think-marker result used the wrong marker. We ran it again with `<|start_think|>` (token 128002) and a `Reasoning: /think` system line.
- The trace-likelihood comparison first showed the Snowball SFT as the most-penalized author. The analysis found two causes, and neither cause was style:
  - The first cleanup cut each response at role lines that start a line. It did not remove role words joined to the answer text.
  - The traces were sampled at temperature 1.0.

  We ran the decode ablation to control for these causes. After the ablation, the SFT ties with Kimi-Linear as the most-penalized author.
- We added `<|im_end|>` as a stop token in a separate cohort. We changed nothing else from run `2026.10.31.23`.

## Conclusion

New bases contain the assistant format before post-training. Post-training mostly narrows a small number of positions, for example the think tag at the assistant turn. For the Qwen3.5 base, the main agentic bottleneck was the turn stop, not knowledge of the format.

Evaluation results for checkpoints without sampling defaults depend on the serving path. PR [#10906](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10906) adds `generation_config.json` defaults to Marin HF exports. Evalchemy local chat requests still need explicit `--gen_kwargs`.
